INCREASE IN MSP 
1529. SHRI IMRAN MASOOD: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण 
मंğी be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Government has evaluated the actual benefits of the increase in the 
Minimum Support Price (MSP) announced for 14 Kharif crops for the year 2026-27; 
(b)  if so, the State-wise details of the number of farmers who got an opportunity to sell 
their produce at the MSP; 
(c)  whether the Government is aware that farmers in several States were compelled to 
sell their produce at prices lower than the MSP; 
(d)  whether the Government is formulating any new action plan to strengthen the 
effective and universal procurement mechanism at MSP; and 
(e)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b):  The Government announced the  Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 14 Kharif 
crops for the Kharif Marketing Season (KMS)  2026-27 in the month of May, 2026.  
Procurement for these kharif crops usually begins after harvesting in October–November 
each year. 
(c) to (e): Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 
mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations of 
the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of the 
State Governments and Central Ministries/Departments concerned.  
While recommending MSPs, CACP considers important factors like cost of 
production, overall demand-supply situation of various crops in domestic and world 
markets, domestic and international prices, inter-crop price parity, terms of trade between 
agricultural and non-agricultural sector, likely effect of price policy on rest of the economy 
and a minimum of 50 percent as the margin over cost of production. 

Government offers to procure agricultural crops through designated procurement 
agencies and farmers have the option to sell their produce to the government agencies or in 
the open market whichever is advantageous to them.  
Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement by 
Government agencies when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Government 
procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India (FCI) and other 
designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. Procurement of pulses, 
oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under umbrella scheme of 
Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), on the request of the 
concerned State Government as per the guidelines as and when market price of these 
produce fall below the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-AASHA Scheme are 
National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd (NAFED) and National 
Co-operative Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton and Jute are also 
procured by Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute 
Corporation of India (JCI), respectively. 
In addition, Adequate number of procurement centres are opened by respective 
State Government Agencies, taking into account the production, marketable surplus, 
convenience of farmers and availability of other logistics / infrastructure such as storage 
and transportation etc. Temporary purchase centres, in addition to the existing mandis and 
depots/godowns are also established at key points. The procurement operation is a 
continuously evolving process and during the last few years, procurement processes under 
MSP have improved to ensure payment of MSP to farmer’s bank account directly and 
linkage of Aadhaar and land records with the States’ procurement portals ensure that the 
farmers directly get the benefits of the MSP purchase.  
  
Government has launched Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses till 2030-31, to 
reduce import dependence and achieve self-sufficiency in pulses.To encourage domestic 
production of pulses, the Government is undertaking procurement of Tur, Urad and Masur 
under the PM-AASHA Scheme on the request of State Government from pre-registered 
farmers as much as offered by them through Central Nodal Agencies, namely the National 
Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and the National 
Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF). 
Government also implements Market Intervention Scheme (MIS), a component 
under PM-AASHA, for procurement of agricultural and horticultural commodities, which are 
perishable in nature and are not covered under the Price Support Scheme (PSS). The 
objective of intervention is to protect the growers of these commodities from making 
distress sale in the event of a bumper crop during the peak arrival period when the prices 
tend to fall below economic levels and the cost of production. There should be at least a 10 
percent decrease in the ruling market prices over the previous normal year. The scheme is 
implemented at the request of a State/UT government. 
 
Government has introduced a new component of Price Differential 
Payment (PDP) under Market intervention scheme (MIS) from 2024-25 season for direct 
payment of the price difference between the Market Intervention Price (MIP) and the selling 
price to the farmers of perishable crops. States/UTs have an option to choose either to do 

physical procurement of the crop or to make the differential payment between the MIP & 
Sale Price to the farmers. 
 
Further, from 2024-25 season, Government added another component under Market 
intervention scheme (MIS) for reimbursing the Storage and Transportation cost of TOP 
crops (Tomato, Onion and Potato) to central nodal agencies & State designated agencies 
for transporting them from the producing State to consuming states in the interest of the 
farmers.

MEGA HANDLOOM CLUSTER FOR TIRUCHIRAPPALLI 
 
1531.   SHRI DURAI VAIKO: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) whether the Government had approved a Mega Handloom Cluster for Tiruchirappalli under 
the Mega Handloom Cluster Development Programme during 2015 –16 and if so, the details 
thereof;  
(b) the details of present status of implementation of the Mega Handloom Cluster,  including the 
funds released, works completed, ongoing activities and the number of handloom weavers 
benefited so far;  
(c) whether the implementation of the project has been delayed and if so, the reasons therefor; 
and  
(d) whether the Government propose s to release the remaining funds and complete the pending 
infrastructure and livelihood support components under the project, besides strengthening the 
handloom sector in Tiruchirappalli through modernisation, market linkage, skill development 
and common facility centres and if so, the details thereof? 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री(श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) to (d): Yes, the Government of India had approved a Mega Handloom cluster for 
Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) during 2015-16 under Mega Cluster Development Programme, a component 
of National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP), a scheme under implementation through 
Office of Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles all across the country for 
holistic development of the handloom sector.   
 
Trichy Mega Handloom cluster covers 08 districts of Tamil Nadu State i.e. Trichy, Ariyalur, 
Perambalur, Karur, Dindigul, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur & Nagapattinam  benefitting 25462 
weavers.  Financial assistance of Rs.20.17 crore has been released for distribution of 1162 HSS itmes 
for technological upgradation, setting up of 02 Dye Houses with ETP facilities one each at Karur & 
Jayankondam, 01 Souvenir Shop at Thanjavur and 22 Small handloom clusters. 06 Common Facility 
Centre have also been completed and functional at Thiruvidaimaruthur -I, Thiruppanandal, 
Ammapettai, Thathayankarpettai, Karur-I and Thoppampatty.   
 
Besides, Government of India is also providing ma rketing platforms to handloom agencies/ weavers 
to sell their products directly to customers domestic and international level through participation in 
expos, e-commerce portal (https://www.indiahandmade.com), Dilli Haat etc under NHDP. Moreover, 
training for Skill development is also provided under SAMARTH scheme of Ministry of Textiles.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1533 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 28th July, 2026 
 
SUPPORT FOR FARMERS IN AGRICULTURAL DISTRESS 
 
 1533. SHRI K RADHAKRISHNAN: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृͪष एवं ͩकसान 
कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the growing distress among farmers due 
to rising input costs, declining farm-gate prices of several crops and losses caused by 
extreme weather events in recent months; 
(b) if so, the details of the measures taken by the Government to provide immediate 
financial assistance, ensure remunerative prices and compensate farmers for crop 
losses; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to expand the coverage of crop insurance, 
enhance financial support under existing schemes and increase the procurement of crops 
at the Minimum Support Price (MSP); and 
(d) the details of funds released, beneficiaries covered and farmers compensated during 
the last one-year State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (d):  The Government is aware that farmers face challenges due to fluctuations in 
input costs, market prices and climatic conditions. Agriculture is a State subject.  
However, Government of India, through various schemes and programmes supplements 
the efforts of the State Governments in addressing these issues to enhance farmers' 
income, mitigate risks arising from adverse weather events and ensure remunerative 
returns to farmers.  These include:    

(i)   Minimum Support Price (MSP):   Government declares Minimum Support Prices 
(MSPs) for 22 mandated crops, 14 Kharif, 6 Rabi, and 2 commercial crops (jute and 
copra), based on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and 
Prices (CACP) and in consultation with State Governments and Central Ministries. While 
fixing MSP, factors such as cost of production, demand–supply trends, domestic and 
international prices, inter-crop price parity, and terms of trade are taken into account. MSP 
ensures a minimum margin of 50% over the cost of production to the farmers. The 
increase in MSP has significantly benefited farmers, as reflected in the steady rise in 
procurement levels and MSP payments made.  
(ii) Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY): PMFBY provides comprehensive risk 
coverage against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest losses.   
PMFBY along with the Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS), 
provides comprehensive insurance coverage against crop losses arising from natural 
calamities and adverse weather events, thereby mitigating climate-related risks faced by 
farmers.  As on 30.06.2026,   92.68 crore farmer applications have been enrolled under 
PMFBY and RWBCIS, and claims amount of ₹2.02 lakh crore has been paid against 
25.58 crore farmer applications since inception of the schemes in 2016.   About 86% of 
the total unique farmer applications enrolled under the schemes are from small and 
marginal farmers. The State-wise details of funds released, beneficiaries covered and 
claims/assistance provided to farmers during the last one year under the respective 
schemes are maintained scheme-wise and are given in the Annexure.   
 (iii)  State and National Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) In the event of natural 
calamities, relief assistance is provided by the concerned State Governments from the 
State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the approved norms. 
Additional financial assistance from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) is 
provided for disasters of severe nature, following the prescribed procedure. Such 
assistance is in the nature of relief and not compensation.  
(iv)  PM-KISAN:   Under PM-KISAN, eligible farmer families receive income support of 
₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). 
  

In addition, Government is also implementing various other schemes such as the 
National Food Security Mission (NFSM), Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY), Sub-
Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM), Integrated Scheme for Agricultural 
Marketing (ISAM), Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), Formation and Promotion of 
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), and Mission for Integrated Development of 
Horticulture (MIDH), among others, to improve productivity, reduce cost of cultivation and 
strengthen farmers' income.  
    To expand coverage of crop insurance, following steps have been taken by the 
Government under PMFBY:  
 AIDE (App for Intermediary Enrolment), a smart-phone App has been designed 
and rolled out in Kharif 2023 for enrolment of farmers at their door-steps through 
a large network of Insurance Intermediaries. It offers a completely paper-less and 
cash-less experience to a farmer. 
 The Government has actively supported the awareness activities being carried out 
by the States, implementing Insurance Companies, financial institutions, and 
Common Service Centres (CSCs) network to disseminate key features of PMFBY 
amongst farmers and members of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). 
 Further, a structured awareness campaign ‘Crop Insurance Week/Fasal Bima 
Saptah’ has been initiated by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare since 
Kharif 2021 season onwards to increase the awareness about benefits of the 
scheme, sensitize the stakeholders and to increase overall enrolment of farmers, 
with special focus on identified aspirational/tribal districts. Along with this, ‘Fasal 
Bima Pathshalas’ are also being organized at village/GP level for knowledge 
building of farmers on various aspects of scheme implementation.  
 Government had also organized a nationwide Doorstep Crop Insurance 
Policy/receipt Distribution mega drive – ‘Meri Policy Mere Haath’. Hard copies of 
crop insurance policy receipts are distributed to farmers enrolled under PMFBY 
through special camps at gram Panchayat/village level. 
  

 Apart from this, other activities for awareness generation involve the publicity of 
key features and benefits of the scheme through advertisements in leading 
National and local newspapers, airing of audio-visual spots on regional / local 
channels, distribution of IEC material in local languages, dissemination of SMS 
through Kisan / National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) portal and organisation of 
online workshops of all stakeholders including farmers, Panchayat Members, and 
other key stakeholders. 
       The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep 
MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. Accordingly, 
Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial 
crops with a minimum return of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of 
production from year 2018-19 onwards. 
        Government offers to procure agricultural crops through designated procurement 
agencies and farmers have the option to sell their produce to the government agencies 
or in the open market whichever is advantageous to them.  
         Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement by 
Government agencies when market price of these produces falls below the MSP. 
Government procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India (FCI) 
and other designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. 
Procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under 
umbrella scheme of Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), 
on the request of the concerned State Government as per the guidelines as and when 
market price of these produces fall below the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-
AASHA Scheme are National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd 
(NAFED) and National Co-operative Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton 
and Jute are also procured by Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India 
(CCI) and Jute Corporation of India (JCI), respectively. 
       Increased MSP has benefited farmers of the country which are evident from data of 
procurement and MSP amount paid to the farmers. The details of procurement and MSP 
amount paid to farmers during 2004-2014 and 2014-2026 (upto June, 2026) are given as 
under:

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO– 1534 
                                                       ANSWERED ON- 28.07.2026 
  
EMPOWERMENT OF PANCHAYATI RAJ INSTITUTIONS  
  
1534. SHRI SHYAMKUMAR DAULAT BARVE:  
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has assessed the status of financial and administrative 
empowerment of Panchayati Raj Institutions in the country; 
  
(b) whether it is a fact that many Gram Panchayats are facing difficulties in effectively 
implementing local development works due to inadequate financial resources, shortage of 
manpower and limited administrative powers; 
  
(c) the details of funds released by the Central Government to Panchayati Raj Institutions 
along with the mechanism in place for monitoring the utilisation of such funds during the last 
five years, State/Union Territory-wise; and 
  
(d) the steps taken by the Government to provide greater financial autonomy, enhance 
decision-making capacity at the grassroots level and make Gram Panchayats self-reliant? 
  
 
 ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a)        Yes Sir. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has released a report titled “Status of Devolution 
to Panchayats in States - An Indicative Evidence-Based Ranking, 2024” in February 2025 to 
assess the effectiveness of devolution and the role of local governments in strengthening 
grassroots democracy, including assessment of the status of financial and administrative 
empowerment of Panchayats Raj Institutions (PRIs). This report presents the Devolution Index, 
which provides the overall scores and ranks for all States/Union Territories (UTs) covered under 
Part-IX of the Constitution, based on six identified dimensions: Framework, Functions, Finances, 
Functionaries, Capacity Enhancement, and Accountability.  
  
(b)        Yes Sir, many Gram Panchayats are facing difficulties in effectively implementing local 
development works due to inadequate financial resources, shortage of manpower and limited 
administrative powers. “Panchayat”, being “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of 
State List of Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Panchayats are set up and operate 

2 
 
through the respective State Panchayati Raj Acts which may vary from State to State, subject to 
the provisions of the Constitution. Article 243G of the Constitution empowers the Legislature of 
a State to make provisions, by law, for the devolution of power and responsibilities upon 
Panchayat at the appropriate level, subject to such conditions as may be specified, with respect to 
the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice and implementation of 
schemes for economic development and social justice as may be entrusted to them including 
those in relation to matters listed in the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution. The State 
legislatures are to consider the 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule for devolution of 
power and responsibilities to Panchayats. Accordingly, all matters relating to Panchayats, 
including, implementing local development works, manpower requirement, financial resources, 
administrative powers at the Panchayat level and enhancement of the financial and 
administrative autonomy of Panchayats, etc. fall within the purview of State Government. 
  
(c)        During the 15th Finance Commission (FC) award period (FY 2020-21 to FY 2025-26), 
including the interim period of FY 2020-21, a total of Rs. 2,82,632 Crores have been released 
against the total allocation of Rs. 2,97,555 Crores. The State-wise details of allocation & release 
of the funds under 15th FC is placed at Annexure I. Further, under the Revamped Rashtriya 
Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) of the Ministry, a total of Rs. 3601.77 Crores have been released 
to the States/UT during the last five year from FY 2021-22. The details of funds released to the 
States/UTs under the Revamped RGSA scheme during the last five years is at Annexure-II. 
  
 As part of the Digital India initiative, MoPR has established an integrated digital 
governance ecosystem for Panchayats to promote transparency, accountability, and efficient 
financial management. This Ministry has launched ‘eGramSwaraj’ in 2020–21 as a unified 
digital platform which supports end-to-end planning, budgeting, accounting, monitoring, and 
online payments. Its integration with the Public Financial Management System (PFMS), 
Government e-Marketplace (GeM), and AuditOnline has enabled seamless fund flow, 
transparent procurement, payments and auditing, thereby strengthening governance and financial 
oversight at the grassroots. As a result, around 2,40,435 out of 2,64,998 i.e. 90.73% of PRIs have 
generated audit report in FY 2024-25. The tier-wise details of audit report generated in FY 2024-
25 is placed at Annexure-III. 
                                                                                                  
 (d)      The Ministry has implemented the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rashtriya Gram 
Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/ UTs. The main objective of 
the scheme is to build the capacity of PRIs by creating a learning ecosystem, especially through 
training for the Elected Representatives (ERs), functionaries, and other stakeholders to develop 
their governance capabilities to function effectively, and also by supporting exposure visits, 
development of training modules and materials, etc. A total of 1,66,41,509 Elected 
Representatives were trained from FY 2022–23 to FY 2026–27 (as on 10.07.2026) under the 
scheme. 
  
A major step has also been taken to build capacity and train elected representatives and 
functionaries of Panchayats through institutes of excellence such as Indian Institutes of 
Management (IIMs)/ Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) under the Leadership/Management 
Development Program (MDP). Under this MDP training, 3,490 people have been trained so far 
as on 10.07.2026. 

3 
 
  
The Ministry has also implemented the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) under 
RGSA scheme, which has significantly enhanced transparency, efficiency, and governance at the 
grassroots level. The eGramSwaraj application, developed as part of the e-Panchayat MMP, has 
facilitated digital planning, accounting, monitoring, and online payments at the Panchayat level. 
The integration of eGramSwaraj with the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) enables 
real-time payments to vendors and service providers, ensuring seamless fund flow and reducing 
delays. During Financial Year 2025–26, 2,55,254 Gram Panchayats across the country, uploaded 
their Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs).  
  
Further, ‘AuditOnline’, an application has been developed for online audits of Panchayat 
accounts and their financial management. This application has been launched in April 2020 for 
transparent auditing of Central Finance Commission funds utilisation to strengthen financial 
management of Panchayats.  
  
            The Ministry, has also undertaken a significant step to digitise the collection of Own 
Sources of Revenue (OSRs) of the Panchayats by developing the “SAMARTH Panchayat 
portal”, a dedicated digital platform that facilitates the generation of tax & non-tax demands and 
collection thereof, maintenance of tax registers, and online tracking of revenue. This digital 
empowerment is designed to bring transparency, efficiency, and scalability to local financial 
administration. 
  
            In 2025, the Ministry has launched the Atma Nirbhar Panchayat Special Award (ANPSA) 
to promote Atmanirbharta through the augmentation of OSR by Panchayats. 
  
Moreover, to provide greater financial autonomy, enhance decision-making capacity at 
the grassroots level, and make Gram Panchayats self-reliant, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, in 
collaboration with IIM Ahmedabad, has developed a training module on OSR to strengthen the 
financial self-reliance of Gram Panchayats. The module helps elected representatives and 
Panchayat functionaries understand how OSR is generated through tax and non-tax sources. 
Under the Specialised Module of OSR, 2,75,893 have been trained so far as on 10.07.2026. 
  
Further, the Ministry has developed applications such as Meri Panchayat, which have 
endeavoured to bring transparency in Panchayat Governance by making information on 
planning, activities and progress of works in Panchayat accessible to public. Similarly, 
Panchayat NIRNAY is an online application that aims at bringing transparency and better 
management in conduct of Gram Sabhas by Panchayats.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1535 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28th July, 2026 
  
Proposal for Insurance Company 
  
1535.   Prof. Sougata Ray: 
  
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  whether the Government has any proposal to set up insurance company, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b)  the reasons for setting up of another insurance company despite the insurance sector is 
regulated by IRDA; 
(c)  whether a feasibility study or financial viable assessment has been conducted for the 
proposal; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof; and 
 (e)  whether the proposed insurance company will be wholly under the Government or a 
public undertaking or a joint venture with private entities and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
  
(a to e)   In order to realize the vision of Sahakar -se-Samriddhi, Ministry of Cooperation has 
undertaken several initiatives to strengthen the cooperative sector and deepen its reach up to 
the grassroot level across the country. These initiatives are aimed at promoting cooperation 
based economic developmen t model, including socio -economic upliftment of small and 
marginal farmers, traders and other weaker sections. 
  
The Ministry of Cooperation has undertaken several initiatives to enable cooperative 
banks to carry out banking and allied financial activities at par with commercial banks, 
including acting as 'Corporate Agents' for the distribution of insurance products. These 
initiatives are aimed at diversifying the business portfolio of cooperative banks, strengthening 
their financial viability and competitiveness, enhancing fee -based income, and promoti ng 
financial inclusion. Further, these measures have ensured the expansion of access to and 
availability of quality banking and insurance services through the cooperative banking 
network, particularly in rural, semi-urban, and underserved areas. 
 

Page 2 of 2 
 
Further, with the efforts of the Ministry of Cooperation, RBI has also removed the 
requirement of a minimum net worth of ₹50 crore for Rural Cooperative Banks to obtain a 
Corporate Agent licence for the distribution of insurance products, thereby facilitating greater 
participation of cooperative banks in insurance sector and expanding access to insurance 
services.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1536. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 28TH JULY, 2026. 
 
NATIONAL SINGLE WINDOW SYSTEM 
 
1536.  SHRI ASHISH DUBEY: 
SHRI HASMUKHBHAI SOMABHAI PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the major initiatives taken by the Government to strengthen the National Single 
Window System (NSWS) to facilitate industrial approvals; 
 
(b)  the progress made in integrating additional Central Ministries, Departments and 
States with the platform; 
 
(c)  the number of approvals and services currently available through the NSWS 
and the areas covered in it; and 
 
(d)  whether the Government has made any assessment of the impact of the NSWS 
on improving ease of doing business and reducing approval timelines, if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): The Government has undertaken continuous initiatives to strengthen the 
National Single Window System (NSWS) with the objective of providing a single 
interface for business -related approvals and clearances across Central 
Ministries/Departments and States/UTs. In order to facilitate seamless 
industrial approvals, the following key features and enhancements have been 
implemented: 
 Know Your Approvals (KYA) Module : An intelligent tool to enable 
businesses to identify the specific approvals required for their proposed 
operations. 
 Centralized Document Repository: An online repository allowing 
investors to upload documents once  and utilize them across multiple 
applications, thereby eliminating the need for repeated submissions. 
 Common Registration Forms: Standardized application forms introduced 
to simplify and streamline the registration process for investors. 
 

 BharatAssist (AI Chatbot) and Grievance Redressal Mechanism:  An 
AI-enabled chatbot deployed on the platform to assist users and ensure 
efficient resolution of queries, along with an integrated grievance redressal 
mechanism. 
 Enhanced Platform Capabilities: The platform now includes PAN-based 
Single Sign-On (SSO), unified dashboards, integrated payment gateways, 
and BHASHINI integration to provide multilingual support in 22 Indian 
languages. 
 End-to-End API Integration: The platform has progressed towards 
complete digital ization by enabling end -to-end API -based filing for 
identified business approvals. 
 Entitylocker: NSWS is integrated with Entitylocker to enable investors to 
fetch and submit digitally verified documents, ensuring paperless, secure,  
and faster processing of Central and State approvals. 
 
(b) & (c): National Single Window System (NSWS), accessible through nsws.gov.in, is a 
one-stop digital platform for facilitating Government to Business (G2B) 
approvals and investor-related clearances for industry in a streamlined manner 
with transparency and accountability. At present, NSWS is integrated with 32 
Central Ministries/Departments and 34 States/UTs, providing seamless access 
to 325 Central G2B approvals and 2215 State G2B approvals through a single 
platform. 
(d): NSWS provides a single -window platform for businesses to apply for 
registrations, approvals and licenses. All eﬀorts are made to provide a 
seamless experience, however, the timelines for grant of approvals depend 
upon the existing business processes, servi ce delivery mechanisms and 
statutory requirements of the concerned Ministries and Departments. While no 
separate assessment has been done on reduction of approval timelines, NSWS 
has features of dashboards and alerts to Ministries and Departments for 
monitoring the processing of applications, thus increasing transparency and 
enabling timely action.

O.I.H. 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1537 
  ANSWERED ON 28/07/2026 
 
ACTION PLAN UNDER LAKHPATI DIDI INITIATIVE 
 
1537. Shri Bunty Vivek Sahu: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether any special action plan is being implemented under the 
Lakhpati Didi initiative in order to provide entrepreneurship, 
digital financial literacy, bank credit and marketing facilities to 
women of Self-Help Groups in the Chhindwara district of Madhya 
Pradesh; 
(b)  if so, the number of women benefitted from the same till date; 
and 
(c)  whether it is proposed to provide special training, marketing 
support, branding and additional financial assistance for agro-
based processing, forest produce, handicrafts and other rural 
enterprises in view of the local requirement of Chhindwara, if 
so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI)  
  
(a) to (c): Lakhpati Didi initiative is an outcome of Deendayal 
Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), a 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme being implemented by Ministry in 
partnership of States and UTs (except Chandigarh and Delhi), with 
the objective to improve the livelihoods of poor rural households in 
country, and organise rural households into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) 
for their social and financial inclusion.  
  
  Lakhpati Didi initiative is to empower and enable Self-Help Groups 
(SHG) Women, earn a minimum income of Rupees one lakh per annum 
on a sustainable basis, for at least 4 agricultural seasons and/ or 
business cycles. 
 

Page 2 of 3 
 
Under the DAY-NRLM, 10.08 crore rural households have been 
mobilised into around 92 lakh Self Help Groups (SHGs) across the 
country. As on date, more than 3.46 crore SHG members have been 
enabled as Lakhpati Didis. In Madhya Pradesh, 23,67,520 SHG 
members have been enabled as Lakhpati Didis, including around 
46,000 SHG members in Chhindwara district. 
  
   DAY-NRLM is providing entrepreneurship support in the country 
including Madhya Pradesh, through Start-up Village Entrepreneurship 
Programme (SVEP), a sub-scheme under the DAY-NRLM program that 
supports and facilitates the SHGs and their family members to set-up 
small enterprises in the non-farm sector, create an eco-system of 
entrepreneurship in a block by providing trainings and hand-holding 
support through the Community Resource Person for Enterprise 
promotion (CRP-EP), finance through Community Enterprise Fund 
(CEF), domain and business related mentorship. As of June 2026, 4.32 
lakh enterprises have been supported under SVEP in country 
including 30,573 in Madhya Pradesh. 
  
   DAY-NRLM is also providing access to credit and microfinance 
facilities to empower women through various steps which are as 
follows: 
  
(i) Funds are provided to SHGs in the form of Revolving Fund (RF) and 
Community Investment Fund (CIF) to help them in creating a corpus, 
from which the SHG members can avail loans for various purposes. 
  
(ii) The SHGs are also facilitated for Bank linkage for accessing credit 
at subsidized rates of interest. Since 2013-14, the SHGs have been 
assisted to access Bank credit of Rs. 13.41 lakh crores, so far.  
  
(iii) SHG members are also imparted financial literacy skills through 
trainings on accounting, record-keeping, budgeting, and loan 
management etc.  
  
(iv) DAY-NRLM also facilitates universal access to cost-effective and 
reliable financial services to the poor and it works on both demand 
and supply sides of financial inclusion by promoting financial literacy 
among the poor and providing catalytic capital to the SHGs and their 
federations. The promotion of digital finance is done through 
deployment of SHG Women as Banking Correspondent Sakhi (BC 
Sakhi), with the support of banks and Common Service Centers.  
  

Page 3 of 3 
 
Under DAY-NRLM, regular trainings and capacity-building 
programmes are conducted for SHG members and community cadres 
on SHG management, financial literacy, livelihood promotion and 
enterprise development to ensure effective implementation of DAY-
NRLM across all States. 
  
   DAY-NRLM also strengthens market access for SHG products in 
all States/UTs including Madhya Pradesh through a comprehensive 
branding and marketing ecosystem. The Ministry has registered the 
brands “Saras”, “Saras Aajeevika” and “Aajeevika” for promoting SHG 
products, while 25 States have developed their own State-level 
brands, such as UMED (Maharashtra), Palash and Adiva (Jharkhand), 
Himira (Himachal Pradesh) and Mathi (Tamil Nadu).  
   To further enhance market access, Saras Melas are organised 
at the National, Regional, State and District levels, including two 
National-level Saras Melas, one Saras Food Festival and more than 
50 State-level Saras Melas every year. The Ministry also operates the 
Saras Aajeevika Gallery in Central Delhi for the sale of curated SHG 
products, while several States have established permanent retail 
outlets under their respective State brands. In addition, the Ministry 
has developed the eSaras e-commerce platform and partnered with 
GeM, ONDC, Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho and JioMart to expand market 
reach and sales opportunities for SHG products.

ALLOCATION OF BUDGET UNDER DDU-GKY 
 
1538. Dr. Kalanidhi Veeraswamy: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total budget allocation, funds sanctioned and expenditure 
incurred under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya 
Yojana (DDU-GKY), State-wise, including Tamil Nadu; 
(b)  the total number of rural youth trained, certified and placed in 
employment under the Scheme; 
(c)  whether the Government has conducted any assessment 
regarding the quality of training, employability and income 
enhancement of beneficiaries, if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  the measures taken to ensure that women, Scheduled Castes, 
Scheduled Tribes and other disadvantaged groups have 
equitable access to training and placement opportunities; and 
(e)  the steps being taken to strengthen skill development, 
entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihood opportunities for 
rural youth under DDU-GKY? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 (SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
  
(a): Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) 
is one of the cluster of initiatives under Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana 
- National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at livelihood 
diversification and poverty reduction. DDU-GKY aims to skill rural 
youth and promote sustainable livelihoods for rural youth through 
placement-linked skilling programs. The cumulative details of funds 
sanctioned/released and expenditure incurred under DDU-GKY during 
the last five years and the current year are given in Annexure-I. 
  
(b): Under DDUGKY, a total of 18.45 lakh candidates have been 
trained, 11.44 lakh candidates have been certified and 12.35 lakh 
have been placed since inception i.e. 2014-15. 

Page 2 of 3 
 
(c): The quality of training and employability are ensured by the 
scheme design wherein Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) are 
reimbursed allowable funds only after ensuring 6 months of 
employment for at least 70% of the trained and certified 
beneficiaries. Further, an impact assessment study has been 
conducted through Transrural Agri Consulting Services Pvt. Ltd. in 
the year 2025. The income enhancement indicator as per the 
evaluation study has shown that beneficiaries experienced an 
average salary growth of 30.79% in a period of three years with an 
average salary of ₹ 16,500 per month. 
 
(d): DDU-GKY incorporates mandatory social inclusion norms to 
ensure equitable access to training and placement opportunities for 
disadvantaged groups. The Scheme mandates that 50% of candidates 
shall be from SC/ST communities, 33% shall be women, and 3% shall 
be Persons with Disabilities (PwDs).  
 
(e): In order to ensure strengthening skill development, 
entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihood opportunities for rural 
youth under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana 
(DDU-GKY), a number of steps have been taken. These include: 
 Shifting to Batch-Mode payments in place of the earlier project-
mode system, enabling faster and more accountable disbursals. 
 Greater emphasis has been placed on securing a minimum of 6 
months of employment for trained candidates, along with 
tracking support for 12 months to ensure job continuity. Earlier 
a minimum of 3 month of employment was mandated. 
 The scope of the programme has been expanded to include self-
employment and emerging gig economy opportunities, 
promoting entrepreneurial capabilities among the rural youth 
and encouraging local enterprise development.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1539  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28th JULY, 2026 
 
Cooperative Sugar Mill 
1539.  Shri Darshan Singh Choudhary: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that there is not single a cooperative sugar mill in 
Tendukheda Assembly constituency of Narsinghpur district in Madhya Pradesh despite 
having ample potential for sugarcane cultivation; 
(b) whether the Government has received any proposal for the setting up of a cooperative sugar 
mill in the said area or any such proposal is under consideration; 
(c) whether the Government is contemplating for a feasibility study or providing financial 
assistance, technical support or any other necessary assistance for the setting up of a 
cooperative sugar mill in the Tendukheda Assembly Constituency; 
(d) If so, the details of the proposed action plan, estimated cost, financial assistance, timeline 
and the likely benefits to farmer therefrom; and 
(e) If not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
(सहकारिता मंत्री) (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) Yes. As per the information received from  Government of Madhya Pradesh, there is  no 
cooperative sugar mills in Tendukheda Assembly constituency of Narsinghpur district in Madhya 
Pradesh. At present, eight private sugar mills are operational in Narsinghpur district, out of which 
two sugar mills are functioning in the Tendukheda Assembly Constituency.  
 
 

Page 2 of 2 
 
(b) No. The Central Government does not set up  Co-operative Sugar mill in any part of the 
country. As per the information received from Department of Food and Public Distribution, sugar 
industry was deleted from list of industries required compulsory licensing, vide press note dated 
31.08.1998.  
 
(c to e) Ministry of Cooperation has taken up steps to revive co-operative sugar mills in the country. 
National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory organization under the 
administrative control of Ministry of Cooperation provides financial assistance for the revival and 
modernization of cooperative sugar mills either directly to the Cooperative Sugar Mills (CSMs) or 
through the State Government for passing on the same to CSMs, with due-diligence and subject to 
the viability of the project as per NCDC guidelines.

EV CHARGING INFRASTRUCTURE IN LADAKH 
 
1541. SHRI MOHMAD HANEEFA:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the requirement of a comprehensive public Electric 
Vehicle (EV) charging network in the high-altitude and strategically important region of Ladakh, 
particularly along the Leh–Manali and Srinagar–Leh highways;  
 
(b) whether the Government proposes to establish or facilitate EV charging stations at fuel stations 
and other suitable public locations under Central schemes in Ladakh and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) the details of number of public EV charging stations sanctioned a nd made operational in 
Ladakh under various schemes;  
 
(d) whether viability gap funding, capital subsidy or other incentives are being provided for setting 
up charging stations in remote and sparsely populated regions, if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(e) the details of steps being taken to promote electric mobility in the environmentally sensitive 
Himalayan region of Ladakh? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a) to (e): No such assessment has been c arried out by MHI as on 23.07.2026. Setting up of EV 
charging stations (EVCS) is an unlicensed activity and any institution/entity including manufacturers of 
EVs/ EV chargers and private players are free to setup, operate and maintain EVCS across India.   
Under FAME-II scheme, an allocation of Rs.912.50 crore was made for setting up of EV public 
charging stations (EVPCS).  Further, an Rs.2,000 crore has been allocated under the  PM E-DRIVE Scheme 
for deployment of EVPCS on pan India basis, including Ladakh  region. Further, no state-wise allocation 
has been done under the FAME-II scheme.   
Further, no proposal has been received from Ladakh under the PM E-DRIVE scheme.  
 As per information received from 3 Oil Marketing Companies namely BPCL, IOCL and HPCL , 
under the FAME-II scheme, a total of 13 EVPCS have been sanctioned for Ladakh out of which, 12 EVPCS 
are operational as on 01.07.2026.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1542 
  ANSWERED ON 28/07/2026 
 
ALLOCATION OF FUND TO WEST BENGAL UNDER VB-G RAM-G 
 
1542. Shri Adhikari Deepak Dev: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total fund allocated to West Bengal under Viksit Bharat-
Guarantee for Rojgar and Aajeevika Mission-Gramin (VB-G RAM-
G) scheme for the Financial Year 2025-26; 
(b)  whether any fund has been released to the State of West Bengal 
during the last two months, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether any fund has been released to West Bengal which was 
pending for the last three years, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) to (d): The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika 
Mission (Gramin)(VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025 has come into force with 
effect from 1st July, 2026  in rural areas of the entire country 
including in the State of West Bengal. In accordance with the 
provisions of the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, an interim allocation of 
₹8,508 crore has been approved for the State of West Bengal for the 
FY 2026–27 under the scheme. Thereafter, a financial sanction of ₹ 
1264.50 crore, as first installment, have been issued based on the 
demand for funds raised by the State. 
  
The release of funds to the State of West Bengal under Mahatma 
Gandhi NREGS was stopped with effect from 09.03.2022 by invoking 
the provisions of Section 27 of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, owing to continued non-
compliance with the directives of the Central Government by the 
State. Hence, no fund was released to the State during the last three 
financial years. 
  

Page 2 of 2 
 
However, on resumption of implementation of Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS in the State w.e.f.  01.06.2026, Labour Budget for the month 
of June 2026 was approved and Mother Sanction for an amount of Rs. 
346.58 Crore was also issued.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

 ANSWERED ON 28/07/2026 
 
BLUE ECONOMY PROJECTS IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
 
1543.  Dr. Gumma Thanuja Rani: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the details of funds sanctioned and released by the Government to Andhra   
Pradesh under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana and Blue Economy 
initiatives during the last five years, year-wise; 
 
(b) the details of fisheries infrastructure and Blue Economy projects completed in 
Andhra Pradesh during the said period; 
 
(c) whether Government has assessed the impact of the West Asia conflict on seafood   
exports from Andhra Pradesh; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a): The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and 
Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) has been  implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY):  A scheme to bring about Blue Revolution 
through sustainable and responsible development of fisheries sector in India’ in all 
States and Union Territories (UTs) including the State of Andhra Pradesh, since 2020-
21. Under PMMSY, for the development of fisheries and fisheries infrastructure in the 
State, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has approved proposals of 
the Government of Andhra Pradesh at a total cost of Rs 2328.89 crore, with a central 
share of Rs 681.38 crore. An amount of Rs 445.05 Crore has been released to the 
State based on the State's utilization. The year-wise details of projects approved, fund 
sanctioned and released during the last six years under PMMSY for furnished at 
Annexure I. 
(b): The major fisheries infrastructure projects approved under PMMSY for 
development of fisheries in the State of Andhra Pradesh include (i) establishment of 5 
fish feed plants, (ii) 16 cold storages and ice plants, (iii) 6 modern fish landing centres, 
(iv) 3 modern fishing harbours , (v) modernization of fishing harbo ur at 
Vishakhapatnam and (vi) 1 integrated Aqua Park. In addition, 15 Climate Resilient 
Coastal Fishe rmen Villages (CRCFV) and one Fish Brood Bank have also been 
sanctioned.  

(c) and (d):  The Government is closely monitoring developments in the global trade 
environment, including geopolitical situations, through regular engagement with 
stakeholders and ex port promotion agencies. While no separate State -specific 
assessment has been carried out on the impact of the West Asia conflict on seafood 
exports from Andhra Pradesh, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has 
undertaken several initiatives to address emerging trade challenges. These initiatives 
include a Seafood Exporters Meet in April 2026, New Delhi and National Workshop on 
Seafood Exports at Visakhapatnam , Andhra Pradesh  in June 2026, wherein issues 
relating to market diversification, Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), non -tariff barriers, 
traceability, logistics and export competitiveness were deliberated with stakeholders. 
Despite the prevailing global geopolitical and trade  challenges, various efforts taken 
by the Government of India has resulted in India's seafood exports record ing an all-
time high of 19.72 lakh metric tonnes valued at ₹73,890.46 crore (US$ 8.46 billion) 
during the financial year 2025–26.

MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1544 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 28TH JULY, 2026/ SHRAVANA 6, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
CELL BROADCAST ALERT SYSTEM FOR DISASTER WARNINGS 
 
1544.    Ms. SAYANI GHOSH: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the authority or agencies responsible for issuing, 
authorising, operating and  monitoring alerts under the Cell Broadcast Alert 
System for Disaster Warnings system; 
 
(b) the types of disasters and emergencies proposed to be covered under the 
system, the  geographical targeting mechanism adopted and the expected 
lead time within which alerts can be issued prior to such events; 
 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any assessment o f the 
effectiveness of the  system in reducing disaster -related casualties and 
improving emergency preparedness and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the measures taken to ensure that alerts are delivered promptly in 
regional languages  across all mobile networks and handsets, including in 
remote and vulnerable areas? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) Cell Broadcast Alert System for Disaster Warnings is operated  through 
the Integrated Alert System based on the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) 
implemented by National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). The 
system   integrates   five   Warning   Generating   Agencies,  namely the India  
 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 1544 FOR 28.07.2026 
 
 
Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission (CWC), Indian 
National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Defence 
Geoinformatics Research Establishment (DGRE) and Forest Survey of India  
(FSI), with the State Disaste r Management Authorities (SDMAs) of all 
States/UTs. The respective Warning Generating Agencies and SDMAs are 
responsible for issuing and authorising disaster -specific alerts, while the 
CAP-based platform facilitates their dissemination through the Cell Broadcast 
system. 
 
(b) The Cell Broadcast Alert will be used for timely warning to citizens for 
disaster events with very short lead time like Cyclone, Tsunami, Heavy 
Rainfall, Lightning, Flash Flood, Thunderstorms, Hailstorm, Avalanche, 
Cloudburst, Industria l/man-made disasters and other events which merit 
immediate alerting. The Warning generating agencies provide Geo -targeted 
warnings and Geo-targeted alerts are disseminated to the public. 
 
(c) Timely receipt of warning and timely dissemination of alerts acts as one 
of the contributing factor in reducing disaster -related causalities and 
improving emergency preparedness. The System provides timely alerts to the 
public, which indirectly improves emergency preparedness and necessary 
precautions, thus helps in reducing disaster-related casualties. 
 

 
-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 1544 FOR 28.07.2026 
 
(d) All warnings generated by the forecasting agencies are translated to 
the State language of the target population and disseminated to the 
recipients by the SDMAs. The Alerts are received across all mobile networks 
and handsets in the geo-targeted area which includes remote and vulnerable 
areas

      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 28TH JULY, 2026. 
 
NON-AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS FOR STARTUPS 
 
1545.  SHRI RAJKUMAR ROAT: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether the applications of many recognised startups are rejected at the 
incubator level on the ground of "non-availability of funds" or for other reasons 
under the Startup India Seed Fund  Scheme and other Central Startup 
Schemes, if so, the year and State -wise details of applications  received, 
approved and rejected during the last five years, al ong with the reasons for 
such rejections; 
 
(b)  whether the incubators do not provide detailed reasons for rejection of 
applications or any  effective mechanism for appeal or grievance redressal in 
many cases, if so, the action taken by the Government in this regard; and 
 
(c)  whether the Government has any proposals to develop a transparent online 
system to provide information on the status of applications, availability of funds, 
reasons for rejection, facility for appeal and time-bound disposal of grievances, 
so as to ensure that startups, particularly those belonging to Scheduled Tribes 
and remote areas are able to avail the benefits  of these schemes, if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) & (b):  Under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS), financial assistance to 
eligible startups is provided through selected incubators. The Experts Advisory 
Committee (EAC) of SISFS evaluates and selects incubators for  allocation of 
funds. Each selected incubator under the Scheme constitutes an Incubator 
Seed Management Committee (ISMC), that evaluates and selects startups for 
seed support. ISMC determines the quantum and kind of funding (in 
accordance with the guidelines of SISFS) to eligible startups. Therefore, any 
grievances raised by startups, including those related to evaluation of 
applications and disbursement, are examined by the concerned incubator 
selected under SISFS by the EAC. 
The guidelines of the SISFS are available  online at:  
https://www.dpiit.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/eaf3e3bdae9f4d657117f18f6c91
780 a.pdf 

As on 30th June 2026, approved incubators have selected a total of 4,245 
startups for support under the Scheme with a total approved funding of Rs. 
706.33 crore. The State/Union Territory (UT)-wise details of startups supported 
by selected incubators under the Scheme in the last five years viz. 2021, 2022, 
2023, 2024, and 2025 are placed as Annexure-I. 
Further, other Central Startup Schemes supporting incubation, such as TIDE 
2.0 (Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs) Scheme, 
GENESIS (Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups) Scheme, Atal Innovation 
Mission (AIM), National  Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations 
(NIDHI) programmes, A Schem e for Promotion of Innovation, Rural Industry 
and Entrepreneurship (ASPIRE), Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance 
Council (BIRAC) programmes, and Innovation and Agri -Entrepreneurship 
Development programme, have specific operational guidelines and framework 
for evaluation and selection of startups by incubators. 
Grievances related to SISFS, and other schemes raised through the 
Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) are 
also examined and appropriate actions are taken as per  extant 
processes/guidelines of CPGRAMS. 
(c):  All programs and Schemes under the Startup India initiative, are implemented 
on a pan- India basis with multiple specific outreach and awareness measures 
undertaken to expand coverage. As detailed in part (a)& (b), Schemes have 
structured frameworks, digital platforms, operational guidelines, and grievance 
redressal mechanisms to ensure startups from across the country can avail 
benefits. 
Specifically for incubation, under SISFS, applicants can apply for seed fu nd 
from any three incubators selected as disbursing partners for the Scheme in 
order of their preference, irrespective of the location of the incubator. 
The Government has also developed a dedicated digital portal for end -to-end 
implementation of SISFS, pr oviding a common online platform for application 
processing, fund management and monitoring across the country. Benefits 
under the Scheme are further disseminated through various outreach and 
social media initiatives. 
Capacity-building workshops and handho lding support for incubators are 
undertaken to promote eﬀective implementation. Eﬀorts are also undertaken to 
assist incubators and startups, particularly from non -metropolitan regions, in 
navigating the application process. In addition, specific initiativ es for regional 
awareness and outreach of benefits under Startup India initiative including 
SISFS are undertaken through the States' Startup Ranking exercise, Innovation 
Week and TEJAS (Transforming Entrepreneurial Journeys Across States & 
Districts). 
 
********

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1546 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28th July, 2026 
 
EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN FARMERS  
 
1546. SHRI ASADUDDIN OWAISI: 
  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृͪष एवं ͩकसान 
कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that approximately 42% of the agricultural 
workforce comprises women, and nearly half of them are unpaid family workers; 
(b) if so, the steps taken by the Government to leverage technology to formalize 
women's agricultural labour and ensure a good income; 
(c) whether the Government is addressing the challenges, like the lack of land 
ownership for women, which restricts access to formalised credit, subsidies, and 
insurance schemes, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Ministry plans to formulate an action plan to leverage the 
International Year of Women Farmers 2026 for the empowerment of women 
agricultural laborers, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी     (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)  
  
(a):     As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the National 
Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation 
(MoSPI), females constituted 59.8 percent of the total workforce engaged in the 
agricultural activities during 2025 (January-December) across the country. During 
the same period 41.1% female workers were engaged in self employed category in 
agriculture.  
  

 
 
(b): Agriculture Technology Management Agency (ATMA) Scheme supports State 
Government's efforts and introduces latest agricultural technologies and good 
agricultural practices in different thematic areas of agriculture and allied sectors to 
farmers including women farmers through different extension activities viz; farmers 
training, demonstrations, exposure visits, kisan mela, mobilization of famers groups 
and organizing Farm Schools. As per ATMA Guidelines, minimum 30% of resources 
meant for programs and activities are required to be allocated to women farmers and 
women extension functionaries. 
  
     Under Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) scheme, in order to 
make farm machinery more accessible and affordable to farmers, financial 
assistance @ 40-50% of the cost of machinery depending on the category of farmers 
is provided for purchase of agricultural machines. For women farmers the financial 
assistance is @ 50% of the cost of machinery. The Farm Machinery Training and 
Testing Institutes (FMTTIs) impart training to women farmers/ Technicians/ 
Engineers/ Unemployed youths/ Machinery manufacturers, etc. on latest technology 
of farm mechanization. 
 
     The Government is implementing Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) scheme to 
promote adoption of new technologies of agriculture and allied sectors through 
technology assessment, demonstration and capacity development among the 
extension functionaries of state governments and farmers including women farmers.  
 
      Indian Council of Agricultural Research-Central Institute for Women in Agriculture 
(ICAR-CIWA), Bhubaneswar provides latest technologies to increase status of 
livelihood of women farmers. It organises various extension activities like field days, 
exhibitions, exposure visits, demonstration, transfer of technologies through mass 
media etc. to acquaint the women farmers with latest technologies. 
 
(c): Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development has recently 
addressed all States to introduce a column for Gender in the Record of Rights. In 
order to extend the benefits of credit, insurance etc. to farmers including women 
farmers, the Department is implementing various schemes.  
 
     The PM-KISAN provides ₹6,000 per year to all eligible farmers through direct 
benefit transfer without gender discrimination, and has significantly benefited women 
farmers as   ensuring transparent and direct financial support to strengthen their 
income and participation in agriculture. A total of 2,18,66,774 women beneficiaries 
received benefits under the 23rd instalment of PM-KISAN Scheme.  
  

 
     Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY) provides for comprehensive risk 
insurance against crop damage from pre-sowing to post-harvest for crops and area 
notified by the concerned State Government. All willing farmers, including 
sharecroppers, tenant and women farmers are eligible to enrol under the scheme. 
Under PMFBY, 21% female farmers are enrolled during 2024-25. 
 
     Under Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (ISAM), subsidy is provided 
for storage infrastructure, and marketing infrastructure other than storage, to the 
eligible beneficiaries including individuals, Group of farmers/growers, Self Help 
Group (SHG), Cooperative Marketing Federation etc. In order to promote women 
farmers and entrepreneurs including women Self Help Groups (SHGs), assistance in 
the form of subsidy is provided to all the women beneficiaries at a higher rate i.e. 
@33.33% instead of 25%.  
 
      Under Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) concessional interest rates 
on short-term agricultural loans are provided to farmers through Kisan Credit Cards 
(KCC). Farmers (including women farmers) can avail Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans 
at a subsidized interest rate of 7% for their working capital requirement. Additionally, 
farmers who repay their loans promptly receive a 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive 
(PRI), effectively reducing the interest rate to 4% per annum. Number of female 
account holders who have benefited from Agricultural credit subsidy under the Kisan 
Credit Card linked Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) for meeting working 
capital requirements are around 22% of 5.4 crores beneficiaries in financial year 
2024-25. 
 
(d): To commemorate the International Year of Women Farmers 2026, Indian 
Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) organized Global Conference on Women in 
Agri-Food Systems (GCWAS-2026) in New Delhi from 12-14 March, 2026. The 
conference served as a global platform for policymakers, researchers practitioners, 
and other stakeholders to deliberate on gender mainstreaming in agri-food system. 
ICAR has developed a comprehensive compendium of case studies and inspiring 
success stories of women’s empowerment and leadership in agriculture. ICAR has 
also developed a Gender Strategy for National Agricultural Research Education and 
Extension System. The strategy aims to foster inclusive innovation ecosystems, 
ensure equitable access to resources and services, and promote women’s 
leadership at all levels of agricultural value chain.

GAIS FOR FISHERMEN 
1548.  Shri Balwant Baswant Wankhade:  
Adv. Adoor Prakash:  
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased 
to state: 
(a)  the details of claims filed, claims approved, claims rejected, claims pending 
and total compensation disbursed under the Group Accident Insurance Scheme 
(GAIS) for fishermen since 2020-21, year, State and UT-wise;  
(b)  the details of fishermen enrolled un der GAIS, active beneficiaries, uninsured 
fishermen households and coverage percentage of the total estimated fishermen 
population, State/UT-wise; and  
(c)  whether the Government has taken any steps in response to the Standing 
Committee’s recommendation of increasing insurance cover under GAIS from 5 lakh 
to at least Rs.10 lakh? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a): The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and 
Dairying. Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY) with a total investment of Rs. 20,750/- crore from the financial year 
2020-21 to till da te for development of fisheries in all States/Union Territories .  The 
scheme inter-alia provides social security measure to fishers, fish workers through 
group accidental insurance coverage to both marine and inland fishers and allied 
fish workers wherein the entire insurance premium amount is shared between the 
Centre  and State in the ratio  of 60:40, 90:10 for the Himalayan & North Eastern 
States and in the case of the Union Territories, the entire premium amount is paid by 
the Centre.  The insurance coverage provided under the PMMSY includes (i) 
Rs.5,00,000/- against death or permanent total  disability, (ii) Rs.2,50,000/ - for 
permanent partial disability and (iii) hospitalization expenses in the event of accident 
for a sum of Rs. 25,000/.  The year wise and State/UT wise details of claims filed, 
claims approved, claims rejected, claims pending, and total compensation disbursed 
under the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) for fishermen since 2020 21 
are furnished at Annexure-I. 
(b)  During the last five years (2021 -22 to 2025 -26) and current finance year 
(2026-27) of the implementation of t he PMMSY, an average of 35.74 lakh active 
fishers have been enrolled under the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS), 
annually. The average State/UT-wise details of fishers enrolled and coverage 
percentage of the total estimated fishermen population  under Group Accident 
Insurance Scheme (GAIS) are furnished at Annexure-II. 

2 
 
(c): Besides, under the erstwhile Blue Revolution scheme, insurance coverage for 
fishers was modest, with relatively lower benefit amounts. Based on the suggestions 
received from State Governments and evaluation of Blue Revolution Scheme, the 
GAIS coverage unde r PMMSY has been significantly enhanced both in scale and 
value to provide increased financial security and risk mitigation to fishers. As such, 
the sum assured has been increased from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh for accidental death or 
permanent total disability, ₹1 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh for permanent partial disability, along 
with ₹10,000/- to Rs. 25,000 hospitalization support, compared to much lower limits 
under the erstwhile Blue Revolution scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1549 
ANSWERED ON 28TH JULY 2026 
 
NATIONAL LIVESTOCK DEVELOPMENT FRAMEWORK FOR VIKSIT BHARAT 
 
1549. SHRI PARSHOTTAMBHAI RUPALA:  
  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to State: 
 
(a) whether the Government has any proposal to enact a comprehensive National Livestock 
Development legislation or policy framework, drawing upon global best practices, including those of 
South Korea and Vanuatu, to transform India's largely unorganized livestock sector into a scientifically 
regulated, competitive industry;  
 
(b) whether the proposed framework will be formulated in consultation with State Governments, 
Veterinary Councils and other stakeholders to promote scientific livestock development and attract 
domestic and foreign investment; and  
 
(c) the steps being taken by the Government to leverage the livestock sector, which provides 
employment to about 20.5 million people, for enhancing farmers' incomes, exports, ensuring nutritional 
security and achieving rural economic growth? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c) No, Sir. As per Article 246(3) of the Constitution, under the distribution of legislative powers 
between the Union and the States, Animal Husbandry is a State subject. 
To supplement the efforts of the States and Union Territories, the Department of Animal Husbandry & 
Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, is implementing various schemes and policy interventions for 
the comprehensive development of the livestock sector encompassing enhancement of exports, ensuring 
nutritional security and achieving rural economic growth.  The k ey initiatives include the Rashtriya 
Gokul Mission (RGM), National Livestock Mission (NLM), Livestock Health and Disease Control 
Programme (LHDCP), National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) and Animal Husbandry 
Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF).  The implementation of these measures together with the 
efforts of the State and UTs  have contributed to robust growth in the sector . Milk production in the 
country has increased from 146.31 Million Tonnes in 2014-15 to 248.87 Million Tonnes in 2024-25 that 
is by 70 %. Egg production in the country has increased from 78.48 Billion Nos. in 2014-15 to 149.11 
Billion Nos. in 2024-25 that by 90%.  
Further, export promotion and certification of livestock products including value added dairy products 
is mandated to the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) 
and Export Inspection Council (EIC) under Ministry of Commerce and Industry. DAHD has also taken 
up the issues related to export and market access of Indian Dairy products with various countries 
bilaterally through various platform such as Joint Working Group (JWG), Technical Working Group 

etc. Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), Government of India in collaboration with 
the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), has developed the Bharat Pashudhan database based 
on a unique 12 -digit Tag ID to enable livestock traceability and promote exports of value -added 
livestock products. Government of India is encouraging investments through schemes such as Animal 
Husbandry Infrastructure Development Funds (AHIDF) and National Livestock Mission (NLM) which 
aim to strengthen value chains, enhance productivity, and expand market access. Furt her, Livestock 
Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP)  is an initiative of the Department towards creating 
disease-free zones in the country thereby creating market opportunity for export of livestock products.

1550. Shri Hanuman Beniwal: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी   be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that the initial cost of cultivation for horticultural 
crops such as orange and Kinnow and cash crops such as Cumin and Isabgol is very high, 
whereas the rate of agricultural input subsidy is very low, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has received any proposals from various States including 
Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab regarding an increase in the input subsidy 
for such crops and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government intends to increase the limit of agricultural input subsidy in the event 
of crop damage for horticultural crops like orange and Kinnow and cash crops like Cumin and 
Isabgol from Rs. 22,500 per hectare to a minimum of Rs. 750,000 per hectare; and 
(d) if so, the time by which the rules will be amended in this regard and if not, the reasons 
therefor?

THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) and (b): The cost of cultivation of horticultural crops such as orange, kinnow and cash crops 
like cumin and isabgol, is input and labour intensive due to requirement of quality planting 
material, fertilizers, irrigation systems and post-harvest infrastructure. On the requests received 
from various stakeholders and considering the increase in prices of various inputs and materials 
in the horticulture sector, operational guidelines of the Mission for Integrated Development of 
Horticulture (MIDH) scheme were revised in 2025. Under the revised guidelines, the cost norms 

of various horticultural crops were enhanced, along with the introduction of the latest 
technologies used in the horticulture sector. A comparative statement on enhanced support is 
as per Annexure. 
 
(c) and (d): As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State Government 
is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures on ground level in the wake of 
notified calamities. The State Governments undertake relief measures in the wake of natural 
calamities from funds available in the form of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in 
accordance with the Government of India approved items and norms. Additional financial 
assistance, over and above SDRF, is considered from the National Disaster Response Fund 
(NDRF) for natural calamities of ‘severe nature’ and is approved on the basis of a Memorandum 
received from the State Government, in accordance with established procedures. The financial 
assistance provided under SDRF and NDRF is by way of relief and not as compensation. The 
detailed items and norms are available on the Disaster Management Division of the Ministry of 
Home Affairs website: ndmindia.mha.gov.in.
