CLIMATE-RESILIENT MIXED PLANTATION SYSTEMS 
 
1551.  SHRI CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA: 
  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government has reviewed climate-resilient mixed plantation systems 
and the present scientific, scheme and field status in the State of Karnataka, with district-
level data including Dakshina Kannada; 
(b)  the details of the area, farmers, funds, facilities, demonstrations and measurable 
outcomes during the last three years; 
(c)  the details of unit-cost, diagnostic, extension, input-supply and implementation gaps; 
and 
(d)  the decision and timeline for a scientifically aligned, adequately funded intervention?  
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR ) 
 
(a) & (b): As reported by the State Government of Karnataka, there is no specific 
scheme for climate resilient mixed plantation system in Karnataka State.  The major 
plantation crops grown in the State are Arecanut, Coconut, Cashew, Cocoa and Oilpalm in 
an area of 14 lakh hectares. Climate resilient mixed plantation systems involving crops like 
coconut, arecanut, pepper, cocoa, nutmug, cinnamon, banana and other crops are 
encourgaged under various schemes to improve farmers income and enhance resilience to 
climate variability to promote sustainable land use.  Farmers are encouraged to adopt 
plantation based cropping system as climate resilient measure.  These include intercrops, 

cover crops, border crops, shade crops, mixed crops and multilevel cropping systems. 
Cocoa, Pepper, Nutmug, Cardamom, Ginger, Banana are grown as intercrops in Arecanut 
gardens. Pepper, Cocoa, Mangosteen, Jowar, Ragi and seasonal vegetable crops are 
grown as intercrops in coconut orchards. Teak, Silver oak, Mahagani, Melia dubia etc., are 
grown as border crops.  Arecanut, Coconut, Coffee, Cocoa, and Oil Palm are integrated 
with compatible intercrops under mixed plantation systems. This diversity acts as a natural 
biological buffer, reducing the impact of droughts, floods, pests and diseases. Deep rooted 
trees improve water and nutrient uptake, while intercrops efficiently utilize the upper soil 
layers. The system enhances soil health, conserves moisture, increases bio-diversity 
reduces production risks and provides farmers with diversified and year-around income. 
      Further drip and micro-sprinkler irrigation systems are being adopted on a large scale 
for the precise and direct application of water to the root zone, thereby reducing 
microclimate temperature during the summer. This practice conserves water while 
enhancing the growth, development, and yield of fruit and vegetable crops. During the last 
three years, a total expenditure of Rs. 1,047 crore has been incurred, covering 148,577 ha 
under the drip irrigation system benefiting 158,232 farmers. 
The application of foliar nutrition is also being promoted, wherein the spraying of 
potassium and calcium enhances drought tolerance in vegetable crops. The application of 
micronutrients and secondary nutrients through foliar spraying has been recommended to 
farmers to improve crop yield and quality. Foliar application of nutrients during water-stress 
conditions facilitates the rapid absorption of nutrients, thereby promoting better crop growth. 
Farmers are being encouraged to adopt rainwater harvesting through construction of 
farm ponds. These farm ponds enable farmers to utilize stored water during summer and 
drought periods for protective irrigation, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of drought.   
During the last three years, 2,704 farm ponds have been constructed with financial 
assistance of Rs. 3,655 lakh provided. 
Mulching practices, using either organic crop residues or plastic mulch, are being 
promoted for efficient moisture conservation, weed suppression, and the maintenance of 
soil structure. The application of lime to correct soil acidity is also being practiced in high-
rainfall regions, where excessive leaching results in acidic soils. 
These cultivation practices are followed in the major plantation crops growing districts 
such as Shimoga, Chikkamagaluru, Uttara Kannada, Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Hassan, 
Mandya, Mysore, Chitradurga, Bengaluru South, Tumkur, Kodagu. 

(c):     Since State Government is implementing schemes in convergence for climate 
resilient plantation systems, the details of unit cost, diagnostic, extension, input supply and 
implementation gaps are not maintained centrally. 
(d): The Government through, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is 
implementing a project- National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) in 651 
districts that studies the impact of climate change on agriculture and conducts district level 
risk & vulnerability assessment due to climate change including the State of Karnataka. This 
is a scientifically aligned intervention. 
  Out of the 310 districts identified as vulnerable to climate change under the project, 
201 have been categorized as 'High' climate-vulnerable and 109 as 'Very High' climate-
vulnerable. Of the 201 'High' climate-vulnerable districts, 12 districts, namely Bagalkot, 
Gulbarga, Bidar, Koppal, Dharwad, Bellary, Tumkur, Kolar, Bangalore (Rural), Hassan, 
Mysore, and Chamarajanagar, fall in the State of Karnataka. Of the 109 'Very High' climate-
vulnerable districts, 3 districts, namely Gadag, Haveri, and Chitradurga, fall in the State of 
Karnataka. To combat recurring rainfall deficits in Karnataka, location specific climate 
resilient technologies, such as, crop and cropping systems including climate resilient mixed 
planation systems, livestock production system were demonstrated to farmers in 
Chamarajanagar, Chikkaballpur, Chitradurga, Gadag, Gulbarga, Haveri and Tumkur 
Districts, apart from capacity building of the farmers.

(a) the objectives and key features of BharatTradeNet, particularly with regard to 
digitisation and integration of India's international trade ecosystem; 
(b) the extent of integration of the platform with Customs, logistics providers,

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA)  (a) to (d) BharatTradeNet (BTN), announced in the Union Budget 2025–26, is envisaged as a digital public infrastructure for international trade aimed at facilitating digitisation of trade documentation, enabling interoperable exchange of trade-related data and supporting efficient delivery of services across India’s international trade ecosystem. 
The initiative also seeks to establish common standards, digital interfaces and trust 
frameworks to facilitate secure exchange and cross-border recognition of electronic 
trade documents through identity management and trust services. 
BTN will support interoperability and digital interaction among stakeholders in the 
international trade ecosystem, including customs authorities, banks, logistics service 
providers and other trade facilitation agencies, while leveraging their existing digital 
systems and infrastructure. 

2 
 
By consolidating trade documentation and financing solutions onto a singledigital 
platform and interconnecting key stakeholders BTN will eliminate paper-based 
procedures, reduce duplication and compliance delays, and enable single-window 
clearance for exporters and importers. This is expected to lower transaction and 
logistics costs, shorten turnaround times for trade finance, and thereby enhance the 
global competitiveness of Indian goods. 
For MSMEs in particular, BTN's standardised and transparent data infrastructure will 
allow financial institutions to assess risk more accurately and extend timely, 
contextual trade finance, improving credit accessibility for smaller exporters. 
As a horizontal digital infrastructure, BharatTradeNet is not envisaged to be sector-
or geography-specific and is intended to cater to all sectors and stakeholders of trade 
ecosystem. 
The institutional framework and financial outlay for implementation of 
BharatTradeNet, including the contribution of the Central Government and other 
participating entities are under examination and will be finalised duly following the 
prescribed approval process.

THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) & (b): Rajasthan has significant potential for the cultivation and collection  of Milkweed 
across the State.  The Government through Northern India Textile Research Association 
(NITRA) has undertaken extensive research and development technologies for making Milkweed 
suitable for production of sleeping bags, jackets, socks, towels, hygiene products, oil absorbent s, 
vegan leather, medical textiles, etc. 
(c): Under the National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM), 8 R&D Projects have been 
undertaken to promote research, innovation, standardization, technology development and 
commercialization of new age fibres. NITRA has also established partnerships with industries, 
research institutions, State Governments, and community organizations to facilitate 
commercialization and value chain development of New Age/ alternative fibre. The Government 
has also approved a financial  outlay of Rs. 300 crores to promote research, technology 
development and commercialization of New Age Fibres under component III of Kapas Kanti 
Mission .  
(d): The Government through NITRA has initiated pilot activities in Rajasthan in 
collaboration with Women Self -Help Groups involving the collection of naturally available 
Milkweed pods to ensure the supply of raw material for fibre production along with employment  
generation and livelihood opportunities. Also, NITRA has established industry collaborations 
and signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) with leading textile companies for the 
development and commercialization of Milkweed-based products.

1557.  SHRI ANANTA NAYAK: 
   SHRI RAVINDRA SHUKLA ALIAS RAVI KISHAN: 
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state: 
 (a) the progress made in expanding the national crude steelmaking capacity towards 
the target of 300 MTPA by 2030; 
 
(b) the volume of finished steel consumption recorded across the infrastructure and 
manufacturing sectors during the first quarter of the last financial year; 
 
(c) the implementation status of digital tracking mechanisms and emissions monitoring 
systems in the steel sector; and

Infrastructure (30%), Engineering, Appliances & Packaging (17%), Automobile (11%), 
and Other sectors (5%).

ALLOCATION OF FUNDS FOR TAMIL NADU UNDER PMMSY 
1558.  SHRI ROBERT BRUCE C:  
Will the Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying be pleased to state: 
(a) the reasons for Rs. 1,240.95 crore in total project outlays approved for Tamil Nadu under the 
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), the actual central share released stands at a 
severe deficit; 
(b) the details of absolute quantum of central funds physically disbursed directly to traditional and 
artisanal fishermen in Tamil Nadu, year -wise during the last three years and district -wise 
including Tirunelveli; 
(c) whet her the record -high central allocation under the current Union Budget will feature 
dedicated tranches for deep-sea fishing vessel conversions and modernizing fish landing centers 
in southern Tamil Nadu; and 
(d) what immediate financial relief and input -subsidy measures are being initiated by the 
Government to safeguard artisanal fishing families from severe fuel and operational input cost 
inflation? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a): The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) accorded administrative 
approvals for the implementation of projects under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY) in Tamil Nadu during the period 2020 -21 to 2025-26 with a total approved outlay of 
Rs.1,240.5778 crore. This comprise d a Central share of Rs.480.0906 crore, State share of 
Rs.455.6139 crore, and beneficiary contribution of Rs.272.8488 crore covering both Beneficiary 
and Non -Beneficiary components. The approved project out lay represents the total financial 
allocation for the entire scheme period, whereas the Central share is released in phases by the 
DoF, GoI based on the progress of implementation, submission of Utilisation Certificates (UCs), 
and compliance with scheme guidelines, etc. Accordingly, the Central assistance is released from 
time to time, and it does not represent a deficit in the approved project outlay. 
(b): The details of central funds released under PMMSY to Tamil Nadu, year wise during the last 
three years (2023 -24 to 2025 -26) and the details of central funds released under PMMSY in 
Tirunelveli District of Tamil Nadu are provided at Annexure. The subsidy amounts are directly 
transferred to the beneficiaries bank accounts through Electronic Clearing Service (ECS). 

(c): To promote Deep Sea fishing in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), the DoF, GoI had 
introduced a sub-component namely “Assistance for Deep Sea Fishing” and another component 
of “Conversion of Trawlers into Resource Specific Deep -Sea Fishing Vessels” under the 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) on Blue Revolution implemented from 2015 -2020. These 
sub-components were introduced to provide financial assistance to tra ditional fishermen for 
promotion of  deep-sea fi shing in the coastal States/UTs  including Tamil Nadu . The financial 
assistance to traditional fishermen for acquisition of Deep Sea Fishing Vessels (DSFVs) has also 
been continued under the PMMSY at the rate of 40% subsidy for General Category and 60% 
subsidy for SC/ST/Women beneficiaries. Support for DSFVs is also provided by the DoF, GoI, 
under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF). Under PMMSY, 
financial support is provided to traditional fishers for acquisition of deep -sea fishing vessels 
(DSFVs) as well as for Upgradation of Existing Fishing Vessels for Export Competency. Under 
the schemes of Blue Revolution, PMMSY, and the FIDF, projects amounting to Rs.1,314.81 crore 
have been sanctioned for the acquisition of 1,205 deep -sea fishing vessels by traditional fishers 
including the fishers of the Tamil Nadu State. The development and modernisation of 
infrastructure has been accorded high priority under the schemes implemen ted by the DoF, GoI. 
Infrastructure projects worth Rs 187.9 crores were sanctioned under Blue Revolution Scheme in 
Tamil Nadu , which includes fishing harbour project at Mookaiyur and fish landing centre at 
Kunthukal. Projects worth Rs 155.57 crores have been sanctioned under the PMMSY in T amil 
Nadu, which includes three fishing harbour projects viz. modernization of Chennai fishing 
harbour, upgradation of Pazhayar fishing harbour, maintenance dredging of Colachel fishing 
harbour; and four fish landing centre projects viz. Nettukupam fish landing centre, 
Thazankuppam fish landing centre, Arangankuppam fish landing centre, and Goonankuppam fish 
landing centre. Under Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund  (FIDF) 
scheme, 16 Nos of Fishing Harbours and 57 Fish landing centre have been sanctioned in Tamil 
Nadu at total project cost of Rs.1988.35 crore. 
(d): The subsidy/concession rate on fuel to the fishermen has been provided by the respective 
State Governments/Union Territories, by exercising their powers to frame their own taxation and 
welfare policies for the fisheries sector. It is informed by the State Government of Tamil Nadu 
that the Government is providing sales tax exempted diesel to the fishermen for reducing  the 
operational cost of their fishing boats (Both mechanized fishing boats and motorized country 
crafts) and also providing subsidized industrial kerosene to the motorized country crafts operated 
in the districts of Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari districts.  
Under these scheme, Government of Tamil Nadu is providing sales tax exempted diesel of  19,000 
L / year / craft to 4,500 Mechanised fishing boats, sales tax exempted diesel of  4,400 L / year / 
craft to 13,500 Motorized country crafts and s ubsidized industrial kerosene of 3,700 L / year / 
craft to around 7500 Motorized country crafts.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): With a view to strengthen its multipronged strategy in 
addressing the rural poverty through a defined roadmap for 
comprehensive development of rural infrastructure and employment 
generation, the Government has introduced The Viksit Bharat - 
Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) 
Act, 2025 with effect from 1st July, 2026 in rural areas of the entire 
country including Bihar.  Out of the budget allocation (BE 2026-27) of 
Rs.95,692 crore under VB- G RAM G, Rs.6,715 crore has been

(c) to (e) : The Government periodically reviews the implementation 
and outcomes of its key rural development programmes to ensure 
enhanced livelihood opportunities, improved rural infrastructure, and 
socio-economic stability, including in Bihar. To address the 
challenges of over-dependence on agriculture, rural youth migration 
and livelihood instability, the Government has taken a multi-pronged 
approach under various flagship rural development schemes, 
ensuring both livelihood diversification and enhanced social security 
for rural households.  Besides, Ministry of Rural Development has 
evolved a comprehensive multi-level and multi-format system of 
monitoring and evaluation of rural development schemes, including 
Performance Review Committee Meetings, National Level Monitors 
(NLMs), Area Officers Schemes, Common Review Mission, Concurrent 
Evaluation and Impact Assessment Studies. State specific reviews of

measures such as digital solutions, regular coordination with State 
Governments, grievance redressal mechanism, provision for social

i. The primary objective of this Act is to align the rural 
development framework with the national vision of Viksit

employment guarantee of one hundred and twenty-five days in

National Rural Infrastructure Stack, with a thematic focus on

infrastructure, livelihood-related infrastructure and special 
works to mitigate extreme weather events. 
iii. To facilitate adequate farm-labour availability during peak

whole of government delivery through Viksit Gram Panchayat 
Plans, integrated with the PM Gati Shakti to address the varying 
needs of Gram Panchayats, powered by geospatial systems, 
digital public infrastructure, district and State planning 
mechanisms, with such plans aggregated at the Block, District,

v. To modernise governance, accountability and citizen 
engagement through a comprehensive digital ecosystem, 
including biometric authentication at various levels, global 
positioning system or mobile based worksite monitoring, real 
time management information system dashboards, proactive 
public disclosures and the use of Artificial Intelligence for 
planning, audits and fraud risk mitigation.

FARMER SUICIDES DUE TO DEBT 
 
1561. SMT. HARSIMRAT KAUR BADAL: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS क ृ िष और िकसान कʞाण मंũी be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that farmer suicides linked to debt continue to be 
reported from Punjab; 
(b) whether any comprehensive and updated data on farmer suicides linked to indebtedness 
is maintained at the national and State level; 
(c) if so, the details of the total number of farmer suicides reported in the State of Punjab 
during each of the last five years (2022–2026), the primary causes identified in each year 
and the compensation paid to next of kin of farmers who died by suicide; and  
(d) whether the Government has any plan for legal recognition and comprehensive 
implementation of the MS Swaminathan Commission recommendation for an MSP equivalent 
to at least C2 cost plus 50% profit, which farmer unions in Punjab have consistently 
demanded as the only lasting solution to the debt-crisis?

कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1562 
ANSWERED ON 28.07.2026 
 
EV POLICY 
 
1562. SHRI CHAMALA KIRAN KUMAR REDDY:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether EV Policy goes beyond purchase incentives, laying out a clear road map for structural 
reforms and strengthening the institutional framework in the transport sector and sets structural 
roadmap for clean mobility, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) the details of budgetary allocation for its implementation and an overall investment outlay aimed 
at accelerating the transition to electric mobility through a mix of incentives and 70 infrastructure 
expansion;  
 
(c) whether the new policy is more compre hensive and will gradually transform the entire transport 
system towards electric mobility; and  
 
(d) if so, the details thereof including present targets set/achieved for 2047, State -wise along with 
funds sanctioned, spent and policy decisions taken by States especially Telangana? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a): Yes. While demand-side schemes like FAME-II and PM E-DRIVE focus on reducing upfront 
costs, the institutional framework is strengthened through supply-side Production Linked Incentive 
(PLI) schemes for the Automobile and Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) sectors, which mandate high 
technology adoption and Domestic Val ue Addition (DVA) . Furthermore, the Phased 
Manufacturing Programme (PMP) establishes a structural roadmap for indigenisation by requiring 
the domestic manufacturing of critical EV components over time. 
 
(b): The transition is supported by substantial budgetary allocations aimed at simultaneous market 
creation and infrastructure expansion. The FAME-II scheme concluded with a total outlay of ₹11,500 
crore, while the successor PM E-DRIVE scheme has been launched with an allocation of ₹10,900 
crore. To bolster the manufacturing ecosystem, the PLI-Auto scheme features a budgetary outlay of 
₹25,938 crore, and the PLI-ACC scheme provides ₹18,100 crore.  
 
(c): Yes, the new policies are comprehensive. They address demand as well as supply side of 
manufacturing of EVs. 
 
(d): The Central Government has not fixed any specific target for the number of Electric Vehicles 
(EVs) on the road by 2047. However, it is promoting EV adoption through various schemes, namely 
FAME India Scheme Phase -II (₹11,500 crore), PLI Scheme f or Automobile and Auto Components 
(₹25,938 crore), PLI Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage (₹18,100 crore), 
PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) Scheme (₹10,900 
crore), PM e -Bus Sewa –Payment Secur ity Mechanism (PSM) Scheme (₹3,435.33 crore) and the 
Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars in India (SPMEPCI). Several 
States, including Telangana, have also notified dedicated EV policies to complement these initiatives. 
The schemes of the Ministry of Heavy Industries are demand -driven and, therefore, no State -wise 
allocation of funds is made.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE & EMPOWERMENT

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 1563 
                                                                                    TO BE ANSWERED ON – 28/07/2026 
 
REHABILITATION, PALLIATIVE CARE AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY SUPPORT 
FOR DIVYANGJANS 
1563. Sh. M K Raghavan: 
 Will the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment be pleased to state: 
 (a) the details of financial assistance, free medicines, rehabilitation services, physiotherapy, 
occupational therapy, speech therapy and palliative care being  provided to differently abled 
children under various Central Government schemes; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to establish dedicated multidisciplinary paediatric 
rehabilitation and palliative care centres in Government hospitals across the country, 
particularly at the district level, if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the steps taken to strengthen follow-up care for high-risk new-borns and differently abled 
children so as to reduce disability and improve their quality of life? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
(SHRI B. L. VERMA) 
(a):  The details of various Central Government schemes under which financial assistance, free 
medicines, rehabilitation services, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and 
palliative care are being provided to differently abled children are as under:  
i. CDEIC( Cross Disability early intervention sub-scheme) under SIPDA, Department 
of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD): The CDEIC sub-scheme 
provides screening, early identification, referral, Speech Therapy, Occupational 
Therapy, Physiotherapy and parental/peer counselling for children with disabilities in 
the 0–6 years age group. The scheme does not provide direct financial assistance. 
ii. Scholarship Scheme for Students with Disabilities, DEPwD: The scheme provides 
financial assistance through six scholarship components—Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top 
Class, National Fellowship, National Overseas Scholarship and Free Coaching. During 

2 
 
the last five years, scholarships amounting to ₹636.74 crore have been disbursed to 
1,73,585 students with disabilities. 
iii. Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances 
(ADIP) Scheme, DEPwD: The scheme provides modern aids and appliances to children 
with disabilities to improve their functional capabilities. It does not provide direct 
financial assistance. 
iv. Disha and Vikaas Schemes implemented by  National Trust: The Disha and Vikaas 
schemes provide physiotherapy, occupational therapy and speech therapy services for 
children with disabilities. No direct financial assistance is provided under these 
schemes. 
v. National Health Mission (NHM), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare: Under 
NHM, States and Union Territories receive technical and financial support to strengthen 
public healthcare services. Ayushman Arogya Mandirs provide comprehensive 
healthcare services, while the Free Drugs Service Initiative (FDSI) ensures free 
essential medicines and helps reduce out-of-pocket expenditure. 
(b): No such proposal is under consideration at present.  
(c): The Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) is 
implementing the Cross Disability Early Intervention Centre (CDEIC) sub-scheme under the 
Scheme for Implementation of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (SIPDA). The CDEICs 
provide screening, early identification, referral, therapeutic services (Speech Therapy, 
Occupational Therapy and Physiotherapy) and parental/peer counselling for children with 
disabilities in the 0–6 years age group. Follow-up care is strengthened through robust referral 
networks, multidisciplinary early intervention, developmental monitoring, individualized 
rehabilitation plans, regular therapy, caregiver training, digital follow-up tools, frontline 
worker capacity building, community awareness, and coordinated rehabilitation services, 
ensuring continuity of care and improved developmental outcomes.

UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1564 
ANSWERED ON 28.07.2026 
  
DEVELOPMENT OF DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE IN PANCHAYATS 
  
1564. SHRI VIJAYAKUMAR ALIAS VIJAY VASANTH:  
                    
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has taken steps to improve connectivity between Panchayats and 
cities, if so, the details thereof including roads, transport and digital infrastructure developed and 
if not, the reasons therefor; 
  
(b) whether any district-wise plan exists to enhance rural-urban connectivity, if so, the details 
thereof and if not, the reasons for lack of integrated planning linking Panchayats with nearby 
urban centres; 
  
(c) whether schemes like rural roads and transport services have achieved desired connectivity 
outcomes, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons for gaps affecting rural mobility and 
access; 
  
(d) whether adequate funds have been allocated for improving Panchayat to city connectivity, if 
so, the details thereof State-wise and if not, the reasons for insufficient funding impacting 
infrastructure development; and 
  
(e) whether the Government has ensured last-mile connectivity from Panchayats to major cities, 
if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons for continued gaps in transportation networks? 
 
  
ANSWER 
 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) to (e): This subject matter does not come under the purview of Ministry of Panchayati Raj.  
  
However, the Ministry, under the revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) scheme, 
supports strengthening of digital infrastructure of Panchayats by providing computer facilities 
and through co-location of Common Service Centres (CSCs) in Panchayat office premises on a 
limited scale to facilitate service delivery. For the period 2022–26, under the Scheme, approval 

2 
 
was accorded for a total of 65,345 computers and for co-location of 17,547 Common Service 
Centres (CSCs) in Panchayat office premises across 29 States and 5 Union Territories. 
  
Further, for promotion of eGovernance in the Panchayats, under the Digital India initiative, the 
Ministry of Panchayati Raj has developed various digital platforms and applications to bring in 
transparency, accountability and efficiency in local rural governance of the country. This 
Ministry has launched eGramSwaraj (https://egramswaraj.gov.in), a user friendly web-based 
portal, which aims to bring in better transparency in the decentralized planning, progress 
reporting, financial management, work-based accounting and details of assets created. The 
application has been further integrated with Public Fund Management System, Government e-
Marketplace, AuditOnline applications for smooth payment, transparent procurement, and 
auditing of Panchayats accounts. 
  
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) has also undertaken a significant step to digitise the 
OSR collection of the Panchayats by developing the “SAMARTH Panchayat portal”, a dedicated 
digital platform that facilitates the generation of tax & non-tax demands and collection thereof, 
maintenance of tax registers, and online tracking of revenue. This digital empowerment is 
designed to bring transparency, efficiency, and scalability to local financial administration.

INCENTIVES AND SUPPORT TO RAGI FARMERS 
  
1565. SHRI YADUVEER WADIYAR: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of Central incentives and support measures provided to Ragi (Finger 
Millet) farmers in the Mysuru and Mandya regions of Karnataka, including MSP operations, 
input support, crop diversification schemes and procurement levels during the last three 
years; 
(b) the total quantity of Ragi procured from these regions under Central schemes and 
the corresponding financial outlay; 
(c) whether the Government has established or approved any dedicated millet export 
hubs, processing clusters, or value-addition centres in Karnataka to promote global trade in 
millets; 
(d) if so, the details of such hubs, including locations, implementing agencies and 
operational status; and 
(e) the details of the steps taken to strengthen branding, GI-based promotion and 
international market access for Karnataka’s millets? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) is implementing a 
Sub-Mission on Nutri-cereals (Shree Anna) under the National Food Security & Nutrition 
Mission (NFSNM) to increase the production and productivity of millets (including Ragi). 
NFSNM-Nutri cereals is being implemented in Karnataka and assistance is provided to the 
farmers, through the States/UTs, for demonstration on crop production and protection 
technologies, for production and distribution of certified seeds, for Integrated Nutrient and 
Pest Management measures, for capacity building of farmers through cropping system-
based trainings, etc. Flexibility has been given to States / UTs to identify districts for 
implementation of different components of the Mission prioritizing districts with low 
productivity but high potential. 
The Department of Agriculture, State Government of Karnataka has informed that 
under NFSNM, 13,518 hectares have been covered under demonstration for Ragi and 
7,004 quintals of certified seeds of Ragi have been distributed during 2023-24 to 2025-26 in 

Mandya and Mysuru districts. In addition, 65,567 hectares have been covered under 
integrated nutrient and pest management for all millets during 2023-24 to 2025-26 in 
Mandya and Mysuru districts.  
The ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (IIMR), Hyderabad through its 
scientific, technological as well as varietal development provides support for finger millet 
cultivation including multilocational evaluations conducted under AICRPs. During 2014-25, 
Central Varietal Release Committee (CVRC) has released 276 Millets varieties including 49 
varieties of Finger Millet for cultivation in different agro-ecologies of country. 
The Department of Agriculture, State Government of Karnataka has also informed 
that Karnataka is one of the DCP (Decentralised Procurement) State for Minimum Support 
Price (MSP). Ragi is procured at MSP declared by Government of India every year. 
Procurement is done through authorized Purchase Centres opened at Taluk and hobli level 
(based on requirement) in Mysuru and Mandya districts. The Department of Agriculture, 
State Government of Karnataka has informed that 76450.35 metric tonnes amounting to 
Rs.356.23 Crores of Ragi was procured in Mysuru and Mandya during 2025-26. 
The state government is also implementing the Crop Diversification Programme 
under Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) to promote alternative 
crops for replacing tobacco farming with other agricultural/horticultural crops in the districts 
of Belgavi, Hassan and Mysuru.  
(c) & (d): The Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka has informed that 
millet-processing clusters and value addition centres have been established and organic & 
millet hubs to facilitate marketing opportunities including exports have been approved. The 
state government has informed that it has facilitated the establishment of 15 Regional 
Organic Federations, of which 10 are exclusively engaged in the procurement, processing 
and marketing of millets. In addition, a Centre of Excellence on Small Millets has been 
established at the University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Bengaluru to address primary 
and secondary processing, entrepreneurship development, training, product development 
and market facilitation. Further, the ICAR-IIMR, Hyderabad is functioning as the Global 
Centre of Excellence (Shree Anna), actively facilitating technical backstopping, capacity 
building, and technological standardization for millet processing and value addition. ICAR 
has informed that the institute also supports start up incubations and processing enterprise 
models across millet-growing states, including Karnataka. 
(e): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries is implementing the Production Linked 
Incentive Scheme for Millet-Based Products (PLISMBP) to increase the use of millets in 
food products and promote their value addition by incentivizing the manufacturing and sale 
of selected millet-based products in both domestic and export markets. Seven units of Millet 
based products approved under the scheme are situated in Karnataka. 
The state government has informed that the Prime Minister Formalization of Micro 
Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme is being implemented in the state by the 
Karnataka State Agricultural Produce Processing & Export Corporation Limited (KAPPEC). 
Under the scheme, to establish a micro food processing enterprise, beneficiaries are 
eligible for a 35% credit-linked subsidy, along with an additional 15% subsidy from the State 
Government, making the total subsidy available up to 50%. 3076 units have been 
sanctioned for establishment of Millet Processing Units in the state. Further, for promotion 

of export market for millets, KAPPEC organises Export Training Programmes, B2B and 
participation in Domestic and International Trade Fairs to facilitate Market Linkages. Under 
the Karnataka Raitha Samruddhi Yojana, 19 brands have been created for millets. 
 Towards export promotion, the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export 
Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag off of the first consignment of value-
added products of millets from Karnataka to Australia under the India-Australia Economic 
Cooperation Trade Agreement (ECTA) in 2022 and to New Zealand in 2026. Further, 
APEDA along with various organisations had undertaken more than 10 capacity-building 
initiatives for FPOs, startups, women entrepreneurs and food processors and to address 
key interventions for agricultural development and export enhancement in Karnataka 
including Brainstorming training programmes for new entrepreneurs, start-ups and FPOs on 
millets in 2026.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †1566 
ANSWERED ON 28/07/2026 
  
MODEL WOMEN-FRIENDLY GRAM PANCHAYAT SCHEME 
  
†1566.SHRI SANJAY UTTAMRAO DESHMUKH: 
  SHRI SANJAY HARIBHAU JADHAV: 
  SHRI OMPRAKASH BHUPALSINH ALIAS PAVAN RAJENIMBALKAR: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
(a) the key objectives and the details of the Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats initiative; 
(b) the manner in which these Panchayats are proposed to be selected and developed in each 
district; 
(c) the steps being taken to ensure effective participation of women representatives in the 
workshops and follow-up initiatives and the district-wise details thereof, in particular of 
Maharashtra; 
(d) the manner in which long-term policy changes at the ground level are being ensured through 
the outcomes of the said workshops along with the steps taken in this regard; and 
(e) whether there is any set mechanism in place to share best practices and experiences for 
elected women representatives to promote women-led governance in various States through a 
collaborative approach, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) and (b) Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj 
Abhiyan (RGSA), the Ministry has taken up capacity building of Panchayati Raj Institutions 
(PRIs) through training of Elected Representatives (ERs), including Women Elected 
Representatives (WERs), functionaries, and other stakeholders to enhance their leadership and 
governance capabilities. 
  
As part of this effort, the Ministry launched the Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan during the 
National Workshop held on 4–5th March 2025 in New Delhi to empower Women Panchayat 
Leaders with knowledge and skills on various aspects of rural governance. The campaign also 
saw the launch of the Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayat (MWFGP) initiative, along with 
other initiatives for Women-Led Development.  In line with the broader objective of saturating 

2 
 
all Gram Panchayats in the country across all nine themes of the Localization of Sustainable 
Development Goals (LSDGs), the MWFGP initiative aims to create an inclusive and gender 
sensitive local governance system that ensures women’s participation, safety, rights, and 
empowerment at the grassroots level towards the attainment of Theme 9: Women-Friendly 
Panchayat. These MWFGPs will act as learning centres for replication of the interventions made 
by them among other Gram Panchayats subsequently. 
  
States/UTs have been advised to identify one Gram Panchayat in each district for transformation 
into a Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayat (MWFGP), in consultation with the relevant line 
departments, and it was also advised to consider the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 1.0 
score as one of the selection criteria for the same. In pursuance of this direction from the 
Ministry, 32 States/UTs have identified 744 Gram Panchayats as MWFGPs. 
(c) & (d) 2-Day National Workshop on Best Practices of Model Women Friendly Gram 
Panchayat was organized on 8-9 January 2026 at YASHADA, Maharashtra. A total of 216 
participants from 13 States/UT have attended the said workshop. Review & Follow-up meetings 
with the participating States/UT have been held to ensure effective participation in the workshop. 
Out of 216, 87 participants from 34 Districts of Maharashtra have participated in the said 
workshop.  
Furthermore, the Ministry has advised the States/UTs to organise Conventions of Women 
Elected Representatives (WERs) to showcase the exemplary practices of women Panchayat 
leaders, as well as Quarterly Review Meetings on the progress of Model Women-Friendly Gram 
Panchayats (MWFGPs) to assess and monitor their performance. During FY 2025–26 and FY 
2026–27 (up to 10 July 2026), a total of 29,567 Women Elected Representatives (WERs) 
participated in the Women Elected Representatives Conventions organized across the country. 
Out of these, 3,531 WERs participated in the Conventions held in the State of Maharashtra 
during the said period. 
In addition, a total of 7,772 representatives of MWFGPs have attended Quarterly Review 
Meetings in the FY 2025-26 to 2026-27 (as on 10th July 2026), and 422 representatives have 
participated from Maharashtra during the said reporting period.  
The outcomes of the workshops on MWFGP are being institutionalized through capacity 
building of Women Elected Representatives, integration of a gender-responsive plan into the 
Gram Panchayat Development Plan, and development of a repository of exemplary cases to scale 
up best practices for ensuring policy and institutional changes at the grassroots level.  
(e) Yes, Sir. Best Practices of the Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats and various 
initiatives of Women-Led Governance undertaken by women elected representatives have been 
disseminated at the National & State Levels through workshops, training programmes, and 
seminars.  
In addition, a National Conference on the occasion of International Women’s Day for Women 
Elected Representatives was organized on 11th March 2026. The conference witnessed the 
exemplary practices of Model Women Friendly Gram Panchayats across the country, and the 
launch of the Compendium of Best Practices on MWFGPs.

Non-Registration of West Bengal Cooperatives 
 
1567. Shri Jagannath Sarkar: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a)   whether it is a fact that cooperative societies of West Bengal have not been registered on 
the portals of NCCF (National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India), NAFED, NCOL 
(National Cooperative Organics Limited), NCEL (National Cooperative Exports Limited) and 
BBSSL (Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited), if so, the details thereof; 
(b)   the consequent loss to West Bengal farmers in terms of denial of access to consumer retail 
networks, MSP procurement, organic certification, international export markets and affordable 
certified seeds respectively; and 
(c)    the steps taken by the Government to ensure West Bengal cooperatives are onboarded on 
all five platforms and the timeline fixed therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
 सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
(a) & (b): 
i. No Sir, the e -samyukti portal of National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India 
(NCCF) and e-samridhi portal of National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation 
(NAFED) are open digital platforms on which all eligible PACS, Cooperative Societies, 
FPOs and farmers can register at any time. There are no state or region specific restrictions

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No- 1569 
ANSWERED ON 28/07/2026  
 
NATIONAL SCHEME OF WELFARE OF FISHERMEN 
 
1569. KM SUDHA R : 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to 
state:  
(a)  whether the National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen provides financial assistance 
to fishermen, if so, the details thereof since 2020, year and State-wise;  
(b)  the details of number of houses and c ommunity halls for recreation and work 
purposes built for the benefit of fishermen under the scheme since 2020, State-wise;  
(c)  the number of houses and community halls have been built for fishermen in Lok 
Sabha Constituency Mayiladuthurai in Tamil Nadu, which has about 71 km of coast; and  
(d)  the details of procedure particularly Mayiladuthurai to apply for and obtain houses, 
community halls and tubewells for fishermen in Lok Sabha Constituency Mayiladuthurai and 
who is the nodal officer in Tamil Nadu? 
 
ANSWER 
 THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
  (SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a):  The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying 
is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana” (PMMSY) with a total outlay 
of Rs. 20,750 crore , with effect from 2020 -21 for holistic development of fisheries and 
aquaculture sector in all States/ Union Territories.  The scheme inter-alia envisages several 
welfare related activi ties for fishers and fish farmers  like (i) development of Integrated 
Modern Coastal Fishing Villages in the maritime States/UTs with an aim to maximize 
economic and social benefits to coastal fishers while minimizing environmental degradation 
through susta inable fishing practices, (ii) insurance coverage of Rs.5.00 lakh against 
accidental death or permanent total disability, Rs. 2.50 lakh against accidental permanent 
partial disability and Rs. 25,000 against accidental hospitalization in the age group of 18  to 
70 years, (iii)  livelihood and nutritional support for socio -economically backward active 
traditional fishers families for conservation of fish resources during fishing ban/lean period 
in the age group of 18 to 60 years wherein assistance  is provided  @Rs.3000/- per fishers 
and beneficiaries’ own contribution of Rs.1500/ - for three months during fishing ban/lean 
period in the ratio of 50:50 for general state,80:20 for North Eastern States and Himalayan 
States while 100% for UTs.  (iv)   the National Rollout Plan of Vessel Communication and 
Support System under the PMMSY scheme including installation of transponders on 

1,00,000 fishing vessels in all Coastal States and Union Territories with a total outlay of Rs. 
364.00 Crore  which enhances the safety of  fishermen and their vessels  The State -wise 
details of Integrated Modern Coastal Fishing Village approved, Group Accident insurance 
coverage provided, Livelihood and Nutritional support and Transponders distributed are at 
Annexure-I, II, III and IV respectively.   
 
(b) and (c):  Under the ongoing Scheme on PMMSY, there is no such housing scheme for 
fisherman being implemented centrally. However, Government of Tamil Nadu has reported 
that under the Fishermen Housing Scheme of their State plan, 2883 houses have been 
constructed which includes 19 fishermen houses in Mayiladuthurai Lok Sabha Constituency 
in Tamil Nadu since the year 2020. 
(d): As reported by Government of Tamil Nadu, the eligible fishermen may apply for 
assistance under the Fishermen Housing Scheme by submitting the prescribed appli cation 
along with the required documents such as (i) A copy of the Aadhaar Card, (ii) Family Smart 
Card, (iii) Fishermen Cooperative Society Membership Card and (iv) Land ownership 
document (Patta/Land Deed), to the Assistant Director of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare, 
Mayiladuthurai.  The Assistant Director of Fisheries scru tinizes the applications  and the 
eligible applications are forwarded to the Director of Fisheries Chennai. The Directorate, 
after due scrutiny, recommends the eligible applications to the Director of Rural 
Development and Panchayat Raj Department. Thereafter, the applications are forwarded to 
the Concerned District Rural Development Agency (DRDA). The Concerned Block 
Development Officer (BDO) conducts a field inspection to verify the applicant's land 
ownership and eligibility. Based on the verification repo rt and subject to fulfilment of the 
prescribed norms, the DRDA sanctions and allots the house to the eligible beneficiary.  
However, no projects relating to the construction of community halls or bore wells (tube 
wells) have been implemented in the Mayiladuthurai Lok Sabha Constituency.

(b): Under PMGSY, funds are released to States/ UTs as a whole and 
not to Constituencies/ Districts separately. During Financial Year 
2021-22 to 2026-27 (till 23.07.2026), Central funds of Rs. 3,044.62 
crore have been released to State of Assam under PMGSY. During the

flood prone, however, no PMGSY road has suffered any major flood

restoration works, is in progress.

projects is the responsibility of the State Government within the 
timeline of the scheme. However, the Ministry of Rural Development 
has taken a number of initiatives to expedite completion of road 
works sanctioned under PMGSY, some of which are given below:- 
i. Programme is regularly monitored by way of Regional Review 
Meetings (RRMs), Performance Review Committee (PRC) 
Meetings, Monthly review meetings and Pre-
Empowered/Empowered Committee Meetings with the States. 
ii. The State Governments are also regularly advised to convene 
meetings with the concerned authorities to expedite matters 
relating to land issues, forest clearances etc., to expedite 
completion of works. 

Page 3 of 4 
 
iii. States have been requested to augment execution capacity and 
contracting capacity, and their compliance in this regard is 
regularly reviewed. 
iv. Training is imparted to field engineers and contractors, as well 
as their staff, for capacity building. 
v. The Ministry has also conducted a number of Contractor’s 
Outreach Programmes in the States to attract the contractors 
in the implementation of PMGSY projects. 
  
As per PMGSY guidelines, ensuring the quality of road works is the 
responsibility of the State Governments who are implementing the 
programme. The Government has established a robust three-tier 
Quality Assurance Mechanism to independently verify that PMGSY 
roads meet prescribed technical standards, including durability and 
resilience to climatic stress:  
 First Tier (In-house): The Programme Implementation Units 
(PIUs) are responsible for process control through mandatory 
tests on materials and workmanship at field laboratories 
established by contractors. 
 Second Tier (Independent State Level): Independent State 
Quality Monitors (SQMs) conduct structured inspections at 
three critical stages: initial, middle, and final stages of 
construction. 
 Third Tier (Independent Central Level): The National Quality 
Monitors (NQMs), who are retired senior engineers, perform 
unannounced, random inspections across districts. Their role is 
to provide an objective third-party audit of the work quality and 
the effectiveness of the state’s quality control system.  
Further, as per programme guidelines, maintenance of roads 
constructed under the programme is the responsibility of the State 
Governments.  All road works sanctioned under the scheme are 
covered by initial five year maintenance contracts to be entered into 
along with the construction contract, with the same contractor, as 
per the Standard Bidding Document. Maintenance funds are to be 
provided by the States/ UTs. Even after 5 years, the roads are to be 
maintained by the States/UTs. Ministry has implemented Electronic 
Maintenance of Rural Roads under PMGSY (e-MARG) in all States/UTs 
to enhance focus on maintenance of roads constructed under PMGSY 

Page 4 of 4 
 
and also to streamline the delivery of routine maintenance of PMGSY 
roads. 
Further, to ensure Climate Resilience & Durability the following 
measures are in place: 
 Design Vetting: All Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) are vetted 
by State Technical Agencies (STAs) (like NITs/IITs) to ensure 
structural designs are suitable for the specific terrain and local 
climate (e.g., higher embankments in flood-prone districts). 
 Green Technology Mandate: Since 2013, It has been made 
mandatory for the States to use New/Green technologies (like 
Waste Plastic, Cold Mix, and Cell Filled Concrete) for 
constructions of roads sanctioned under the scheme. These 
technologies, particularly Waste Plastic, have proven to 
increase resistance to water-induced damages.  
 IRC Standards: Road designs follow the Indian Roads Congress 
(IRC) codes, which include specific provisions for drainage and 
durability in high-rainfall zones.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

VIKSIT GRAM PANCHAYAT PLAN 
 
1571. Shri Raja Ram Singh: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details and at what level Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan (VGPP) 
be framed in the Gram Sabha who have access to Yuktdhara 
portal for making this plan; 
(b)  the manner by which the rozgar sahyaks and computer 
operators work in the country, State-wise; 
(c)  whether the Government has any proposal to carry out any 
capacity building exercises to make Gram Sabhas familiar with 
the Yuktdhara portal, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  whether the mates get enhanced wages in comparison to 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme 
(MGNREGS) considering the enhanced technological barrier 
they have to navigate, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a): Under Section 16 of the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar 
and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025, every Gram 
Panchayat is required to prepare a Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan 
(VGPP) through a participatory planning process. The Gram Sabha 
identifies and prioritises the permissible works required for the 
holistic development of the Gram Panchayat, and the Gram 
Panchayat prepares the VGPP in accordance with the provisions of 
the Act. The approved VGPP is thereafter consolidated at the 
Intermediate and District Panchayat levels for preparation of the 
aggregate Block and District Plans under the Mission. Yuktdhara is a 
GIS-based planning support tool that assists authorised functionaries 
in scientific planning by providing geospatial information and 
analytical inputs for the identification, prioritisation and planning of 
permissible works, thereby supporting the preparation of the VGPP. 

Page 2 of 2 
 
Access to the Yuktdhara portal is provided to authorised 
functionaries designated by the respective State Governments/Union 
Territory Administrations in accordance with the prescribed 
operational framework. 
  
(b): As per Section 21 of the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar 
and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025, the State 
Government is responsible for providing the necessary staff and 
technical support, including Rozgar Sahayaks and Computer 
Operators, to the District Programme Coordinator and the Programme 
Officer for the effective implementation of the Programme. These 
matters such as the manner by which the rozgar sahayaks and 
computer operators work fall within the administrative domain of the 
respective States/Union Territories. 
  
(c): The Ministry accords high priority to capacity building of all 
stakeholders for effective implementation of VB–G RAM G. Training 
programmes are being organised at the National, State, District, 
Block and Gram Panchayat levels through a cascading training 
framework covering the preparation of Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans 
(VGPPs), technology-enabled planning and monitoring tools including 
use of Yuktdhara. Detailed training modules, user manuals, standard 
operating procedures and digital learning resources like e-Saksham 
have also been made available with the States/Union Territories to 
facilitate effective implementation and strengthen participatory 
planning through Gram Sabhas. Also, Capacity Building is an ongoing 
process and as per the needs and requirements of the States/UTs the 
technical tram send by the Ministry to the respective States/UTs. 
  
(d): Under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika 
Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G, Mates engaged under the Scheme are 
paid wages at the semi-skilled wage rate, as notified by the 
respective State Government/Union Territory Administration in 
accordance with the applicable wage notifications. The wage rates 
payable to Mates are determined by the respective State 
Governments/Union Territory Administrations.

(a) to (e)  Under the Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative, District Export Action 
Plans (DEAPs) are prepared at the district level, eﬀectively subsuming all urban 
centres and towns within that jurisdiction. Accordingly, DEAPs have been formulated 
and adopted for all 52 districts in Madhya Pradesh, including Katni, Panna, and 
Chhatarpur (which covers Khajuraho). These DEAPs are periodically reviewed by 
District Export Promotion Committees (DEPCs) to align with evolving global demand 
and district-specific production strengths. 
 
The specific products identified and prioritized for export promotion in these districts 
are Bricks and Artificial Jewellery for Katni; Crafts and Indian Gooseberry (Amla) for 
Panna; and Handmade Crafts for Chhatarpur (Khajuraho). 
 
The DEH initiative operates as a robust collaborative framework that actively 
converges various ongoing schemes of the Central and State Governments to 
provide comprehensive support and resolve grassroots export bottlenecks. 
 
 
 

2 
 
To assist with quality certification, branding, packaging, and international market 
access, the DEPC acts as a single-window facilitator. Exporters in these districts 
receive assistance through major operational schemes of the Directorate General of 
Foreign Trade (DGFT), such as the Export Promotion of Capital Goods (EPCG) 
Scheme for technology upgradation, Advance Authorisation (AA) for duty-free input 
imports, and the Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) 
Scheme. 
 
Furthermore, the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) systematically strengthens 
export competitiveness, particularly for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
(MSMEs), through two integrated sub-schemes: Niryat Protsahan and Niryat Disha. 
 
Niryat Protsahan facilitates aﬀordable trade finance using instruments such 
as interest subvention, collateral guarantees, and export factoring. Concurrently, 
Niryat Disha enhances market readiness by providing support for export quality and 
technical compliance, international branding, packaging, participation in trade fairs, 
and export warehousing. With this mandate, the India Brand Equity Foundation 
(IBEF) and the Quality Council of India (QCI) have been engaged in developing the 
unified Brand India Framework. 
 
Gaps in logistics, warehousing, and export readiness are systematically 
identified through the consultative DEAP formulation process. Consequently, the 
DEPC integrates local Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Self-Help Groups 
(SHGs), artisan clusters, and MSMEs into the export value chain by mapping their 
products to the district's priority basket and linking them with relevant buyers and 
financial service providers. 
 
For the development of a sustainable export ecosystem, the DGFT has 
partnered with agencies such as the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation (ECGC), 
Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank), Small Industries Development Bank of 
India (SIDBI), Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), and India Post. 
Infrastructure gaps—including cold-chain facilities and freight support—have 
been addressed through scheme convergence. DGFT is also working with Amazon, 
FedEx, Delhivery, DHL, etc., to carry out capacity building programs for exporters to 
onboard them as e-Commerce exporters. Further, awareness programmes are 
being undertaken in collaboration with the Department of Posts regarding the 
procedures and facilities available under Dak Ghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs), with a 
view to enabling exporters, particularly those located in remote and rural areas, to 
undertake exports through the e-commerce route. 
 
Exporter onboarding drives are also being conducted in association with the 
Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) 
and the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA). These initiatives 
are aimed at facilitating small exporters, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and 
Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in overcoming entry barriers and accessing international 
markets directly.

(a) whether the Government is implementing any special scheme or providing assistance to 
promote cooperative agriculture, horticulture and marketing of allied products in the hilly 
States including Uttarakhand; 
(b) if so, the details of financial, technical and marketing assistance being provided thereunder, 
State-wise; 
(c)the number of cooperative societies and farmers benefited from the said schemes so far; and 
(d) the additional steps being taken by the Government to provide access to National and 
International markets to the products of the hilly areas?

सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH)

(i) Yes Sir, the Ministry of Cooperation is providing assistance to promote cooperative 
agriculture, horticulture and marketing of allied products in hilly States, including Uttarakhand 
through National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory  corporation

NCDC during the last five years (2021 -22 to 2025 -26) to the hilly States/UTs, including 
Uttarakhand, are provided at Annexure-I. 
(ii) Establishment of new offices of NCDC in hilly and remote areas, including Jammu & 
Kashmir, Ladakh, Sikkim, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, and 
Nagaland in addition to already existing offices in Assam, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand 
to improve service delivery and market support. 

Page 2 of 4 
 
(iii) Ministry of Cooperation has established Bhartiya Beej Sahkari  Samiti Limited (BBSSL), 
a multi-state cooperative society to provide quality, certified and affordable seeds to farmers. 
So far, BBSSL has signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs ) with Arunachal Pradesh, 
Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, 
Tripura, and Uttarakhand for expanding the availability and marketing of quality seeds under 
the “Bharat Beej” brand across these states. 2,488 quinta ls of quality, certified and affordable

(iv) The steps taken by the Government to provide access to National and International markets 
to the products of hilly areas inter alia, include the following: 
• Establishment of National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL) as an umbrella 
organization to export the goods and services of cooperative societies. So far, NCEL 
has signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs ) with Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, 
Himachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, and Uttarakhand to provide 
access to international markets to the products of the hilly areas. 
• Establishment of National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) as an umbrella 
organization for the procurement, aggregation, certification, testing, branding and 
marketing of organic produce. So far, NCOL has signed Memorandum of 
Understanding (MoUs) with Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & 
Kashmir, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, and Uttarakhand 
to provide market access to the organic products of the hilly areas. NCOL has procured 
around 417 Metric Ton organic  wheat, 40 Metric Ton organic Basmati and 30 Metric 
Ton Sweeteners including Jaggery, Khandsari and Brown Sugar from organic certified 
farmers of Uttarakhand. 
(v) The member cooperative societies of BBSSL, NCEL, and NCOL benefit from access to 
quality, certified, and affordable seeds; assistance in quality testing and certification; access to 
national and international markets; better price realization for their produce; and dividends on 
their shareholding. The state -wise number of cooperative societies that have obtained

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1575 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 28th JULY, 2026 
 
URBAN PERI-URBAN AGRICULTURE 
 
1575. SHRI SANJAY DINA PATIL:    
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of urban and peri-urban 
agriculture in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region with a view to enhancing local food security, 
sustainable farming and efficient utilisation of available land;  
 
(b) the details of schemes implemented for promotion of rooftop farming, protected 
cultivation, organic farming, hydroponics and other climate-resilient agricultural practices 
benefiting farmers and institutions supplying produce to Mumbai;  
 
(c) whether financial assistance or technical support has been extended for promoting 
urban agriculture and farmer collectives in and around Mumbai; and  
 
(d) the measures taken or proposed to strengthen sustainable agriculture, reduce 
transportation costs and enhance the resilience of food supply systems catering to 
Mumbai? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a): As per the information received from State Government, no specific assessment of 
urban and peri-urban agriculture has been undertaken in Mumbai Metropolitan Region.  
 
(b) to (d): The Government is implementing various schemes for promoting  sustainable 
and climate-resilient agriculture in the country including peri-urban areas, under which 
provisions have been made for providing assistance for development of various agriculture 
activities. Under these schemes, the State has to prioritize areas and interventions and 
submit an Annual Action Plan (AAP) annually. Details of such schemes may be seen as 
under:  
(i) Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH): Assistance is 
provided for protected cultivation such as poly-houses, shade-net houses, plastic mulching, 
anti-hail nets, hydroponics, quality planting material, micro irrigation and post-harvest 
infrastructure, including cold storages, pack houses and refrigerated transport to reduce 
transportation costs based on the Annual Action Plans submitted by the State 
Governments. These interventions contribute to enhancing local food production, promoting 
sustainable farming practices and improving efficient utilization of available resources. 

Under the revised Cluster Development Programme implemented under MIDH 
through National Horticulture Board, provision has been made for development of Peri-
urban Vegetable Clusters around major urban centres, including cities such as Mumbai, 
with a view to improving supply chain efficiency, promoting market-linked production and 
mitigating price volatility in fruits and vegetables, including tomato, onion and potato crops. 
Under the scheme, support is provided for protected cultivation, hydroponics, aeroponics, 
micro-irrigation, precision farming, adoption of Good Agricultural Practices, INM/IPM 
practices, traceability, IoT-based solutions and other innovative technologies.   
 
(ii) Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY): For promotion of organic farming, 
Government is implementing Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY), a component of 
Pradhan Mantri- Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY). The PKVY scheme provides 
end-to-end support to organic farmers i.e. from production to processing, certification and 
marketing in cluster-based approach.  
 
(iii) National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF): To promote Natural Farming as 
a sustainable, climate-resilient and environmentally friendly agricultural production system, 
Government of India is implementing a centrally sponsored scheme; the National Mission 
on Natural Farming (NMNF) with the aim to enhance climate sustainability in agriculture by 
promoting location-specific agro-ecological practices that reduce dependency on chemical 
inputs and strengthen natural ecosystems. The scheme is also focus to improve soil 
health and moisture content by encouraging in-situ soil organic matter 
generation through multi-crop systems, biomass mulching, etc. Under the National Mission 
on Natural Farming, financial assistance is provided for the formation of natural farming 
clusters, training and capacity building of farmers, establishment of bio-input resource 
centres, support for preparation of on-farm bio-inputs, Information, monitoring and 
evaluation, certification, branding and market linkages for natural farming produce. The 
Mission also promotes convergence with other schemes of the Department of Agriculture & 
Farmers Welfare and allied Ministries to maximize the impact of natural farming 
interventions and optimize the utilization of available resource for sustainable farming. 
 
(iv) Per Drop More Crop (PDMC): For promotion of micro-irrigation and efficient 
water use, Government is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) of Per Drop 
More Crop (PDMC) in the Country as a component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee 
Yojana (PMKSY). PDMC scheme focuses on enhancing water use efficiency at farm level 
through Micro Irrigation, namely, Drip and Sprinkler Irrigation systems.  
 
(v) Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana: The scheme focuses on 
creation of pre & post-harvest infrastructure in agriculture and allied sectors that help in 
supply of quality inputs, market facilities, etc to farmers. It provides flexibility and autonomy 
to states to implement projects as per the local farmers’ needs and priorities from a bouquet 
of activities in agriculture and allied sectors. The scheme aims to fill the resources gap of 
agriculture and allied sectors by providing financial support to states for undertaking various 
activities to increase in overall growth of agriculture and allied sectors and farmers’ income.

farmers of Aspirational Districts in the country including Shrawasti and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b)  the details of the financial assistance provided to the farmers of the Aspirational 
Districts including Shrawasti under the said schemes during the last five years, year-wise 
and district-wise; 
(c)  whether any assessment has been made by the Government regarding the increase 
in income of the farmers in the Aspirational Districts including Shrawasti as a result of these 
schemes and if so, the details thereof; and  
(d)  the steps being taken by the Government to ensure the expansion of irrigation 
facilities, crop diversification, better marketing of agricultural produce and access to 
markets for the farmers? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): NITI Aayog launched the Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) in January 
2018, wherein, 117 districts were identified as Aspirational Districts. ADP monitors the 
progress of 117 Aspirational Districts including Shrawasti on the basis of 49 Key 
Performance Indicators (KPIs) across sectors such as health & nutrition, education, 
agriculture & water resources, financial inclusion & skill development and basic 
infrastructure.    
Funding under ADP is based on the delta ranking method, which rewards Districts for their 
quarterly progress in the 49 KPIs. The first and second overall rankers are awarded ₹10 
crores and ₹5 crores, respectively, while the top-performing District in each of the five 
sectors receives ₹3 crores. In total, ₹30 crores is awarded quarterly to the best-performing 
districts, irrespective of their States. Financial assistance is not provided to individual 
farmers/beneficiaries. 

(c): Detailed information regarding the performance of all 117 Aspirational Districts including 
Shrawasti on all Indicators is available on the Champions of Change Portal 
(http://championsofchange.gov.in/site/coc-home/), which is in the public domain. The 
performance of Shrawasti District on 18 Indicators relating to Agriculture & Water 
Resources theme is at ANNEXURE-I. 
 
(d): Government implements schemes such as Per Drop More Crop (PDMC), Pradhan 
Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY), Watershed Development Component (WDC) of 
PMKSY and Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-
KUSUM) to improve irrigation infrastructure and water-use efficiency. 
Crop Diversification is being promoted through the National Food Security & Nutrition 
Mission (NFSNM), the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, the National Mission on Edible 
Oil (NMEO) - Oilseeds & Oil Palm, the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture 
(MIDH) by encouraging the production and productivity of crops like Millets, Coarse cereals, 
pulses, oil seeds, oil palm and horticultural crop.  
Government implements Integrated Scheme for Agriculture Marketing (ISAM) and 
Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) to promote creation of scientific storage capacity and 
also for investment in viable projects for post-harvest market infrastructure. National 
Agriculture Market (e-NAM) provides online trading platform for better price discovery 
through competitive online bidding. Farmers Producer Organisations (FPOs) are promoted 
for better collective bargaining and value chain development.

scheme. At the national level, out of the total target of 1.22 crore 
allocated to the States, 97.48 lakh houses have been sanctioned 
under the new phase of PMAY-G. 
  
(b): Since FY 2024-25, a total central share of ₹ 49,407.96 crore has 
been released to the States under PMAY-G. A total of ₹ 88,426.76 
crore has been utilized (including State Government’s matching share 
as per the PMAY-G guidelines). 
  
(c): The State Governments/UT Administrations are the primary 
implementing authorities at the ground level. As reported by the 
States/UTs, the major reasons for delays in completion include cases 
of unwillingness of beneficiaries, permanent migration, disputed 
succession of deceased beneficiaries, delay in allotment of land to 
landless beneficiaries by the States/UTs, at times General/Assembly/ 

Page 2 of 2 
 
Panchayat elections, unavailability of building materials and delay in 
release of funds from State Treasury to State Nodal Account of PMAY-
G. 
  
The Ministry regularly reviews the progress reported by the 
States/UTs and takes up such implementation issues with them for 
timely resolution.
