Page 1 of 6 
 
O.I.H. 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1604 
  ANSWERED ON 28/07/2026 
 
IRREGULARITIES UNDER PMGSY 
 
1604. Shri Babu Singh Kushwaha: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware of the fact that complaints 
have been received regarding irregularities in construction 
quality and the construction of roads without sufficient asphalt 
in rural areas including the Jaunpur Lok Sabha Constituency, if 
so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether it is a fact that despite the records being updated on 
the rural road management portal, farmers, students, and the 
general public are facing difficulties in commuting and meeting 
with accidents due to potholes and the poor quality of several 
roads, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government proposes to revise the norms 
pertaining to the thickness, quality, and load-bearing capacity 
of rural roads, keeping in view the increasing freight traffic, if 
so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to make social audit and 
quality verification by the Gram Sabha mandatory prior to the 
commencement of construction to ensure transparency in road 
construction works, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
  
(a): Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) has an 
institutionalized and rigorous Quality Assurance Framework 
embedded in its Programme Guidelines to ensure that all rural roads 
are constructed in strict conformity with prescribed technical 
specifications and quality standards. As per the PMGSY Guidelines, 

Page 2 of 6 
 
quality is maintained through a mandatory Three-Tier Quality Control 
System: 
1. First Tier (In-House Quality Control): Execution and daily quality 
control are managed by the Programme Implementation Unit 
(PIU). It is mandatory for contractors to set up field laboratories 
at construction sites, maintain Quality Control Registers, and 
pass all prescribed material and workmanship tests prior to the 
release of payments. 
2. Second Tier (Independent State Inspection): Independent 
quality monitoring is periodically carried out by State Quality 
Monitors (SQMs) deployed by the respective State 
Governments. 
3. Third Tier (Independent Central Inspection): Independent and 
random inspections are conducted across all stages of 
execution by National Quality Monitors (NQMs) empanelled by 
the National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA). 
Furthermore, as per Para 15.1 of the PMGSY Guidelines, State 
Governments are primarily responsible for ensuring construction 
quality. Whenever complaints regarding poor quality or irregularities 
are received, they are immediately referred to the State Quality 
Coordinator (SQC) for detailed inquiry and corrective action. If the 
response from the State is delayed or inadequate, NRIDA deputes 
NQMs for independent site inspections, and appropriate follow-up 
action is taken based on their findings. 
In respect of Jaunpur Lok Sabha Constituency, no complaint 
regarding poor construction quality or inadequate use of asphalt in 
PMGSY roads has been received by NRIDA. Further, as per the report 
received from the State Government of Uttar Pradesh, PMGSY road 
works in the rural areas of Jaunpur Lok Sabha Constituency are being 
executed in accordance with approved technical standards and 
adequate asphalt specifications, and no irregularities have been 
reported in these works. 
(b): Complaints regarding potholes, poor road conditions, or 
difficulties faced by farmers, students, and the general public are 
examined and whenever deficiencies are reported or observed, 
necessary action is taken for repair, maintenance, and improvement 
of road conditions as per the applicable guidelines. A statement 
indicating the complaints received through Meri Sadak App for the 
State of Uttar Pradesh during the Financial Years 2025-26 and 2026-
27 (till date) is enclosed as  Annexure-I.  
  

Page 3 of 6 
 
(c): The construction of road works under PMGSY and all its 
verticals are as per the technical specifications and geometric 
design standards given in the Ministry of Rural Development 
Specifications for Rural Roads, Rural Roads Manual of the Indian 
Road Congress (IRC) (IRC: SP:20, IRC: SP:72) and also, where 
required, the Hill Road Manual (IRC: SP:48) and other relevant IRC 
Codes/ Guidelines. 
(d): The scheme relies on a robust quality assurance mechanism, 
pre-construction community consultations, and advanced digital 
transparency frameworks as mandated by the PMGSY Programme 
Guidelines. Details are as under: 
(i) Pre-Construction Consultation and Gram Sabha Approval: As per 
the PMGSY Guidelines, community consultation and local 
participation are mandatory during the planning and Detailed Project 
Report (DPR) preparation stage: 
a. Mandatory Transect Walk: Before finalizing the DPR, a non-
formal "Transect Walk" is organized along the proposed road 
alignment by the Assistant Engineer, accompanied by the 
Panchayat Pradhan/Sarpanch, local Patwari, Junior Engineer, 
and local residents. 
b. Gram Sabha Endorsement: Following the Transect Walk, a 
formal Gram Sabha meeting is convened to discuss local 
concerns, land availability, and alignment issues. The minutes 
of this meeting, recording the resolution of all raised issues, 
along with photographic and videographic evidence of the 
Transect Walk, are mandatorily attached to the finalized DPR. 
(ii)  Transparency and Quality Assurance Measures: To ensure 
continuous public accountability during and after construction, 
PMGSY has embedded multiple transparency and grievance redressal 
mechanisms: 
(a)  Citizen Information Boards (CIBs): Standardized signboards 
displaying project estimates, specifications, execution timelines, 
and contact details of officials are mandatorily installed at all 
construction sites. 
(b) Joint Inspections: Public representatives, including Members of 
Parliament (MPs), Members of Legislative Assemblies (MLAs), and 
Sarpanches, are encouraged to conduct periodic joint inspections of 
ongoing road works. 

Page 4 of 6 
 
(c) Unique Digital Identity & QR-Coding: Under the framework, each 
road will be assigned a geo-spatial identification number linked to a 
QR code. This identity will be displayed on roadside signboards and 
backed by a digital record containing its location, classification, and 
asset details. In effect, every road becomes a traceable, searchable 
entity in a national inventory. On scanning the QR code, the public 
can place the grievance through Meri Sadak mobile application as 
well as the CPGRAMs portal. All the complaints are redressed through 
digital systems in an accountable manner. 
(d) Digital Grievance Redressal: Citizens can directly register 
complaints or quality concerns by scanning the road's QR code via

  Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY ¼okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=h½  be

(a) whether the Government proposes to strengthen coordination between the 
Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) and the Central Board of 
Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) for the timely revalidation and utilisation 
of Duty Credit Scrips in eligible duty drawback and refund cases; 
(b) whether the Government is simplifying export promotion procedures under 
schemes such as Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products 
(RoDTEP) and Rebate of State and Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL) 
through digital integration and paperless processes; 
(c) the details of the assistance provided to exporters, including those in Tamil

okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=ky; esa jkT;ea=h ¼Jh ftfru izlkn½ 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) and Central Board of Indirect 
Taxes and Customs (CBIC) maintain regular institutional coordination and electronic 
data exchange for smooth implementation of export promotion schemes and facilitate 
exporters. 
CBIC prescribes the procedure for re-credit of Duty Credit Scrips in eligible drawback 
and refund cases through issuance of Re-credit Certificates. DGFT and CBIC 
systems are electronically integrated through Indian Customs Electronic Data 
Interchange Gateway (ICEGATE) for verification and utilization of electronic Duty 
Credit Scrips, facilitating seamless processing and reducing manual intervention. 
 
(b) The Government has simplified export promotion procedures under Remission 
of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) and Rebate of State and 
Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL) through digital integration. 

2 
 
 
The operational interface for both schemes is primarily through the Customs 
Automated System/ICEGATE. The exporter indicates the relevant claim at the time 
of filing the shipping bill, and upon processing and validation of eligibility, the benefit 
is scrolled/generated through the Customs system. Duty credit is maintained in the 
electronic duty credit ledger and may be converted into transferable electronic scrips 
in accordance with the Electronic Duty Credit Ledger Regulations, 2021, the entire 
process of generation, maintenance, transfer and utilisation of such credits being 
substantially electronic. 
 
(c) Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) and Central Board of Indirect 
Taxes and Customs (CBIC) regularly undertake stakeholder outreach and awareness 
activities through their field formations, including in Tamil Nadu, by organizing Niryat 
Bandhu programmes, workshops, webinars, and Pahal Sessions to enhance 
awareness and facilitate stakeholder engagement. 
 
(d) The applicable timeline for revalidation and issuance of re-credit in respect 
of Duty Credit Scrips issued under the Foreign Trade Policy is governed by Para 
2.20 of the Hand Book of Procedures 2023 and the Electronic Duty Credit Ledger 
Regulations, 2021. Separately, as regards RoDTEP and RoSCTL, Circular No. 
30/2026-Customs Dated 03.07.2026 has been issued by CBIC for re-credit of the duty 
amount into the electronic credit ledger of the IEC holder, and the procedure for 
claiming refund of customs duties and interest is provided under Section 27 of the 
Customs Act, 1962. 
 
(e) The Government has undertaken various trade facilitation measures to simplify 
export procedures, promote paperless and digital service delivery, reduce transaction 
costs, and improve ease of doing business for exporters. These measures aim to 
enhance the efficiency, transparency and accessibility of trade-related services, 
thereby strengthening India's export ecosystem. To expedite the clearance of export 
consignments, the Government has implemented several automation measures, 
including Auto Let Export Order (LEO) for facilitated Shipping Bills where no 
interdiction has been identified by the Risk Management System, and the use of 
ICETAB (Indian Customs Electronic Gateway), a mobile tablet device that enables 
Customs officers to upload examination reports in real time, thereby minimizing 
manual intervention and expediting cargo clearance processes.

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष और िकसान कʞाण 
मंũी be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to establish a new Agro Processing Cluster 
(APC) in the Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor region to boost the agriculture-based economy 
of Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor; 
(b) whether any new laboratory is proposed to be set up under the Integrated Nutrient 
Management to provide improved seeds and micro-nutrients to the farmers of 
Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor districts; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide special concessions/subsidies to 
small and marginal farmers on modern harvesters and technological equipment for 
sugarcane harvesting; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to implement any special incentive package for 
horticulture and oilseed crops in Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor districts to promote crop

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
क ृ िष और िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a): The Ministry of Food Processing and Industries (MoFPI) is implementing the 
scheme for Creation of Infrastructure for Agro Processing Clusters (APC) across the 
country, as a component of the  Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) for 
development of modern infrastructure to encourage entrepreneurs to set up food 
processing units based on cluster approach . Under the scheme, financial assistance 
in the form of grants-in aid/subsidy @ 35% of the eligible project cost is provided in 
General Areas and 50% of the eligible project cost in North Eastern States including 
Sikkim and difficult areas including Himalayan States (Himachal Pradesh, J&K & 
Uttarakhand), notified ITDP areas and Islands subject to a maximum of Rs. 10.00 
crore.APC scheme is demand-driven in nature, under which applications are invited 
online from the potential investors / entrepreneurs against Expression of Interest (Eol) 
issued by the Ministry from time to time. As on date, there is no project approved in 
Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor districts in the State of Uttar Pradesh under APC scheme. 
 
  

    As per Government of Uttar Pradesh, 50 food processing units have been 
established in Muzaffarnagar district under the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro 
Food Processing Enterprises( PMFME)  Scheme . The PMFME provides credit-linked 
capital subsidies, financial assistance and training to upgrade or set up small food 
processing units. It offers a 35% subsidy on project costs (up to ₹10 lakh), focuses on 
One District One Product (ODOP) items and requires a 10% beneficiary contribution. 
(b): The Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare implements programmes for 
promotion of balanced and integrated nutrient management across the country 
through support for soil testing, soil health management and dissemination of nutrient 
recommendations to farmers. Soil testing laboratories are established and 
strengthened by the States/UTs based on their requirement with assistance under the 
relevant Centrally Sponsored Schemes.  Improved seeds are supplied to the farmers 
under various schemes such as the National Food Security & Nutrition Mission 
(NFSNM), Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Mission for 
Atmanirbharta in Pulses , National Mission on Edible Oils–Oilseeds (NMEO-OS), and 
other crop development programmes. Farmers in Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor are also 
eligible to avail these benefits as per the annual action plans approved for the State of 
Uttar Pradesh. 
(c): The Government promotes agricultural mechanization through the Sub-Mission 
on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) under the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi 
Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) by providing financial assistance to States/UTs for 
distribution of agricultural machinery and equipment, establishment of Custom Hiring 
Centres (CHCs), Farm Machinery Banks and High-Tech Hubs. Assistance is provided 
to eligible farmers, including small and marginal farmers, as per the scheme guidelines 
and the Annual Action Plan approved for the State. 
 
 As per Government of Uttar Pradesh, under SMAM Scheme, farmers are being 
provided with Sugarcane Cutter Planters, Sugarcane Trash Cutters, Tractor-Mounted 
Sugarcane Harvesters, and other specialized agricultural machinery at a 50% subsidy 
for sugarcane harvesting. Harvesters are promoted only through CHCs. As per data 
available on Krishi mapper, total 74 & 22 CHCs has been established under SMAM in 
Muzafarnagar and Bijnor Districts respectively. 
  

 
(d): The Government promotes crop diversification through schemes such as 
the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Mission for 
Atmanirbharta in Pulses, National Food Security & Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) and 
the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oilseeds (NMEO-OS). Financial assistance is 
provided to States/UTs for area expansion, quality planting material, integrated pest 
and nutrient management, post-harvest infrastructure, capacity building and other 
interventions as part of State Annual Action Plans. The Department  has conveyed the 
approval of Annual Action Plan for 2026-27 for Uttar Pradesh wherein projects 
amounting to Rs. 357.29 crore under Sub Mission on Agriculture Mechanisation, Rs. 
26.87 crore under Soil Health and Fertility, Rs. 43.75 crore under Crop Diversification 
Programme, Rs.106 crore under NFSNM, Rs.80 crore under MIDH, Rs.64.06 crore 
under NMEO-OS and Rs.97.18 crore under Mission for Atmanirbharta in Pulses have 
been sanctioned for implementation across various districts of the state. Further, as 
per the Government of Uttar Pradesh, the State Government has launched the 
Mukhyamantri Rajya Audyogik Vikas Mission in February 2026 to promote crop 
diversification through horticultural crops. Under the scheme, farmers are provided 
assistance in the form of subsidy ranging from 25 to 50 percent for various 
components.

कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी    (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)  
(a): Agricultural Marketing is a State subject. Government of India has been supporting 
states to strengthen agricultural marketing and ensure fair and remunerative prices to farmers 
through policy measures and schemes.  
(b): Government of India initiated National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), an all-India 
electronic trading (e-trading) portal by virtually integrating Physical Agricultural Produce 
Market Committees (APMCs). The platform provides farmers access to a larger pool of buyers 
through transparent online bidding, better price discovery and direct payment of sale proceeds 
into their bank accounts. The platform also facilitates inter-State trade by enabling buyers 
across the country to participate in online bidding. As on 30th June, 2026, 1.89 crore farmers 
and 2.78 lakh traders are registered on e-NAM. Inter-State trade on e-NAM has increased 
from 563 MT (₹37 lakh) in 2018-19 to 2,984.3 MT (₹14.28 crore) in 2025-26, with cumulative 
inter-State trade of 28,566 MT valued at ₹83.95 crore. The average number of trader bids per 
lot has increased from 2.1 in 2016-17 to 2.8 in 2025-26, indicating increased competition 
among buyers.  

Under the Central Sector Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer 
Producer Organizations (FPOs), 10,000 FPOs have been registered across the country. The 
FPOs collectivise farmers for aggregation of produce to leverage economies of scale and 
increase bargaining power of member farmers. Since launch of the scheme in 2020, the total 
cumulative turnover of FPOs has crossed Rs.20,340 crore.  
(c): To strengthen post-harvest management, logistics, storage and value addition, under 
Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) Scheme, 12,353 storage infrastructure projects with 
storage capacity of 369.18 lakh MT and 6,901 non-storage projects have been sanctioned in 
last ten years. Under Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) interest subvention support has 
been extended to 18,893 warehouses, 3,110 cold stores/cold chain projects and 2,105 
integrated primary and secondary processing units. Under Mission for Integrated Development 
of Horticulture (MIDH) component, about 1.76 lakh infrastructure units, including pack houses, 
cold storages, refrigerated vans, ripening chambers, pre-cooling and processing units have 
been created.  
Ministry of Food Processing Industries has been implementing Central Sector Umbrella 
Scheme-Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojna (PMKSY) to create, interalia, post-harvest 
infrastructure and processing facilities to boost the overall development of the food processing 
sector. As on 30th June, 2026, 1256 projects have been completed or are operational, 
benefitting about 37.76 lakh farmers.   
 World's Largest Grain Storage Programme is implemented by Ministry of Cooperation 
for storage infrastructure at PACS level, enabling farmers to store produce, avoid distress 
sales, improve access to remunerative markets and reduce dependence on intermediaries. 
Construction work has been completed in 313 PACS creating a storage capacity of 1.80 LMT.    
(d): NITI Aayog in its evaluation report of 2020 and 2025 has recognized the Integrated 
Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (ISAM) as a relevant intervention for strengthening 
agricultural marketing through improved market infrastructure, competitive markets and better 
price realization for farmers. The Scheme has promoted market reforms, FPO-led 
aggregation, value addition and development of post-harvest infrastructure. The reports further 
observe that grading units and storage facilities performed better where integrated with 
horticulture clusters and linked with active FPOs and SHGs, improving utilization and visibility. 
It also noted that more than 60 per cent of beneficiaries reported using post-harvest 
infrastructure and crop processing facilities under ISAM. Beneficiaries recognized 
improvements in price realization, product longevity and market appeal through value addition. 
The evaluation highlighted the potential of e-NAM in promoting transparent markets, efficient 
price discovery, better contract negotiations and improved access to institutional finance. 
Overall, ISAM has contributed to strengthening agricultural marketing infrastructure and 
improving market efficiency.   
(e):  Agriculture is a State subject. Government of India supplements efforts of the States 
through a comprehensive range of Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes and 
programs aimed at increasing production, productivity, farmers’ income etc. across the 
country. These schemes encompass entire spectrum of agriculture, including credit, 
insurance, income support, infrastructure, crops (including horticulture), seeds, mechanization, 
marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer collectives, irrigation, extension, digital 
agriculture and procurement of crops.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1610 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28TH JULY, 2026 
 
PROMOTION OF TRADITIONAL AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE AND SEEDS  
 
1610. SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA:  
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the measures taken by the Government to preserve and promote traditional agricultural 
produce in the country;  
(b) whether the Government proposes to incentivize research work aimed at improving the 
existing indigenous/local varieties of agricultural produce and seeds; and  
(c) if so, the details thereof along with the steps being taken in this direction? 
 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a): The Government has taken several measures for conservation, research, production, 
value addition and promotion of traditional agricultural produce and indigenous/local crop 
varieties in the country. These measures include: 
i. Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), through the National Bureau of Plant 
Genetic Resources (NBPGR) and its network of research institutes, undertakes 
exploration, collection, exchange, characterization, evaluation, conservation and 
documentation of indigenous germplasm. 
ii. Intellectual Property Rights are granted to traditional and farmers’ varieties under the 
Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001. As on 15th July, 2026, 
5346 farmer’s varieties have been registered by PPV&FR Authority belonging to 
traditionally cultivated varieties and landraces. 
  

iii. National Gene Fund has been established under the PPV&FR Act, 2001, with the 
aim of promoting conservation and sustainable use of plant genetic resources, 
including traditional varieties. It seeks to reward and incentivize farmers and 
communities engaged in conservation, improvement, and preservation of plant 
genetic resources through benefit-sharing, awards, and recognition schemes, while 
also supporting capacity building activities to safeguard agro-biodiversity. So far, 45 
Plant Genome Saviour Community Awards, 69 Plant Genome Saviour Farmer 
Reward and 88 Plant Genome Saviour Farmer Recognition have been conferred to 
farmer(s)/ farming communities across the country. 
iv. A component namely "Boosting Seed Production of Traditional Varieties" under the 
Seeds component of the National Food Security & Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) has 
been introduced, aimed at promoting traditional varieties of crops. Under this 
intervention, financial assistance is extended for seed distribution, seed production, 
capacity building, and the creation/development of seed banks for traditional 
varieties, in accordance with prescribed cost norms. 
v. To promote the 'Vocal for Local' initiative in the food processing sector, the PM 
Formalisation of Micro food processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme adopts the 
One District One Product (ODOP) approach, aimed at fostering balanced regional 
development across all districts of the country for supporting district-specific 
agricultural and horticultural products, including traditional and indigenous produce. 
ODOPs have been approved for 726 districts across 35 States/UTs, including 
traditional and indigenous products e.g. Makhana, Shahi Litchi, Jardalu Mango. The 
PMFME Scheme provides financial, technical and business support for processing, 
value addition, packaging, branding and marketing of these products including 
traditional produce. 
vi. Traditional agricultural products possessing unique geographical characteristics are 
also protected through registration under the Geographical Indications of Goods 
(Registration and Protection) Act, 1999, administered by the Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), thereby strengthening their identity, 
branding and market value. 
  

vii. In addition, traditional agricultural products are promoted through commodity-specific 
Boards and agencies such as the Tea Board, Coffee Board, Spices Board, APEDA 
and the National Medicinal Plants Board under their respective schemes for quality 
improvement, branding, value addition, export promotion and market development. 
Recently, Government has established National Makhana Board for production, 
processing, value addition, and marketing of makhana. 
viii. Special thrust has been given to traditional millets ("Shree Anna") through the 
National Food Security and Nutrition Mission, following the observance of the 
International Year of Millets. Indian Institute of Millets Research (ICAR-IIMR) in 
Hyderabad, India, serves as the designated Global Centre of Excellence on Millets 
for promotion of international research and development in millets. 
ix. Under Production Linked Incentive scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI), 
following the UN’s declaration of 2023 as the “International Year of Millets”, a 
dedicated Millet-Base Products (PLISMBP) component was added to incentivize 
value addition and commercialization of millets. 
 
(b) & (c):   Yes, Sir. Government incentivizes and supports research aimed at improving 
indigenous/local varieties of agricultural produce and seeds. The details and steps taken are 
as under: 
i. ICAR-IARI is implementing 13 dedicated research projects, supported by ICAR, DBT 
and DST, for characterization, evaluation and utilization of indigenous germplasm, 
landraces and wild relatives in crops such as wheat, rice, maize, sesame, lentil, 
cucumber and tomato. The projects focus on agrobiodiversity, germplasm evaluation, 
molecular breeding, genomics and genome editing for developing improved, climate-
resilient and disease-resistant crop varieties. 
ii. At ICAR-IARI, research on improving the traditional Basmati varieties has led to the 
development of improved Pusa Basmati rice varieties which accounts for dominant 
share of India’s Basmati exports. 
iii. Two high yielding varieties, namely Pusa Narendra KN1 and Pusa CRD KN2 have 
been released targeting specific Geographical Indication areas in eastern Uttar 
Pradesh, promising improved yield and non-lodging trait against the traditional 
landrace “Kalanamak”.  

iv. ICAR-NBPGR documents genetic resources, maintains inventories and brings them 
into the public domain, facilitating their safe and accelerated use in research and crop 
improvement. This enables researchers and breeders to access indigenous 
germplasm for varietal improvement. As on 15th July, over 1 lakh landraces/traditional 
varieties are conserved in the National Gene Bank. 
v. Under the joint work plan between Alliance Bioversity-CIAT and National Agricultural 
Research System under the aegis of ICAR, promotional activities such as 
documentation of over 5,000 native varieties of 25 crops and evaluation across 11 
states using participatory varietal evaluation (crowdsourcing) is undertaken, resulting 
in the identification of nearly 300 superior traditional varieties for large-scale 
cultivation. Further, nearly 50 Community Seed Banks have been established across 
India, conserving more than 4,000 traditional varieties of over 25 crops under this 
plan. In addition, nutritional profiling of more than 3,000 traditional varieties 
supporting branding and commercialization of indigenous produce and linking it to 
value chains, with brands such as Native Basket, Mountain Grains, Dhartee Naturals 
etc. have also been undertaken. 
vi. Ministry of Food Processing Industries R&D scheme (component of the Human 
Resources & Institutions component of Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana) has 
approved 257 R&D proposals to date – several directed at traditional/indigenous 
produce (millet based products, mahua, drumstick etc.)
